Then when He calls you with one call from the earth, behold, you come forth. Or except by way of establishing the truth and nullifying falsehood. So there must be the fulfillment of His promise of the Romans' victory over the Persians to take their right from them, and there must be that He makes you rise after He has put you to sleep and establishes every right that you saw had been nullified, and nullifies every falsehood that you saw had been put into effect, for He is the most judicious of judges. For if He allowed the killing of a right or the reviving of a falsehood, He would not be as such.

Since they held that this existence is life and death without end, He said: ﴿and a term﴾ that must reach its conclusion, ﴿appointed﴾, meaning in His knowledge from eternity. That term is the time of the establishment of the Hour. That is because just as He set for them terms for their origin and their offspring, and none of them deviated from them, so likewise there must be an appointed term for that from which they were created. When that term comes, this order is dissolved, this firm arrangement is disordered, these judgments cease, these bodies fall apart, and they return to the state of non-existence they were in before. Otherwise the creation would be in vain, and the King, the All-Knowing, is exalted above that.

Since they were denying that they were in disbelief, He emphasized His statement (p-50): ﴿Indeed, many of the people﴾, despite its clarity, ﴿in the meeting with their Lord﴾, who filled them with kindness by their return in the Hereafter to being presented before Him for reward and punishment, ﴿are disbelievers﴾, meaning they are concealers of what is in their intellects of the proofs of His oneness and the evidences of His power and wisdom, concealing it with a great concealment, as if it were an instinct in them. Therefore they deny what God, glory be to Him, has promised you of the Romans' victory over the Persians. So let that not alarm you, for they have already denied what is greater than it, namely the Hereafter, with all the proofs it contains that exceed enumeration. And if you review what preceded in the verse of al-An'am, ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ [al-An'am: 2], you will increase in insight regarding this.

Having established the proof against them, he followed it with warning and terror. He said, conjoining it to "Have they not reflected?": ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth, so that they might see how the end of those before them was?﴾ When the traces of the deniers encompassed Makkah the Honored from east and west, south and north, through the abodes of Thamud, the people of Pharaoh, 'Ad, Saba' and the people of Lut, he named it and made it general, saying: ﴿in the earth﴾, [meaning] a journey of consideration, contemplation and remembrance from whatever direction they wished. This contains an indication that they stop at looking at the outward dominion with their eyes, and fall short of considering the inward dominion (malakut) with their thoughts. It also contains a stirring to them to mount this lofty rank, through this clear expression: ﴿and see﴾.

Since what befell the earlier peoples was a great matter, he drew attention to its greatness by making it fit to be asked about, and said: ﴿how was﴾, meaning a state from which there is no escape, and the masculine form of the verb indicates the greatness of the matter. ﴿the end﴾, meaning the final outcome of ﴿those﴾. Since the condition of those nearer in time to a person is more admonishing to him, he affirmed the preposition and said: ﴿before them﴾, [referring to] the destruction of the disobedient and the deliverance of the obedient. Since knowledge of the outcome is conditioned on knowing the beginning, he said, resuming: ﴿they were﴾, meaning a state which is at the utmost capacity.

[Since the context concerns dominance and victory, which depend on the strength that requires steadfastness, and not on mere numbers devoid of it, he turned away from that and said, omitting the separating pronoun because this context does not show the Arabs' claim to superiority over Persia or Rome]: ﴿much stronger than them﴾, meaning than the Arabs, ﴿in power﴾, meaning in their bodies and their minds. Since the implied sense is: they hewed the mountains and performed, with the most accomplished crafts you see, deeds that no generation approached, he conjoined to it his saying: ﴿and they tilled﴾, by ploughing and otherwise, ﴿the earth﴾, so they brought forth what is in it of benefits, such as waters, minerals, crops and other things, ﴿and they built it﴾, meaning those earlier ones, ﴿more than what they built it﴾, meaning these to whom you were sent. Indeed, they have no great matter in tilling and building the land, for the lands of the Arabs are only black mountains and dusty wastes. This is nothing but mockery of them, and a statement of the weakness of their condition in their worldly life, in which they have no pride apart from it.

Since they had stopped, like these, at the nearest cause, and had not risen with their minds to the highest goal, he informed that He sent to them callers who would alert them from their slumber and rescue them from their heedlessness. The implied sense is: they strayed from the clear path, were blind to the wide way, and deviated from the road of the Lord, so We sent to them messengers. He conjoined to it his saying, indicating by the feminine form of the verb the weakness of their minds through their denial of the messengers, as has been explained at ﴿Those messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253]: ﴿and their messengers came to them﴾, meaning from Us, ﴿with the clear proofs﴾ of miracles, like what your Messenger brought you from Our earlier promises and Our extraordinary affairs, such as the matter of the Night Journey and what appeared in it of wonders, like the announcement that a caravan would arrive on a certain day, preceded by a camel of such a description with such-and-such saddlebags, and so it came to pass. ﴿But they did not believe, just as those who were stronger than you in power did not believe.﴾ ﴿So it was not﴾, meaning because it was not, ﴿that God﴾, with all His attributes of perfection, ﴿would wish﴾ ﴿to wrong them﴾ by doing with them the act of one whom you yourselves would count as a wrongdoer, by destroying them in this world and then exacting retribution from them on the Day of Resurrection before establishing the proof against them by sending messengers with clear proofs. ﴿But they were﴾, with the utmost of their effort, ﴿wronging themselves﴾, meaning themselves in particular, ﴿continually wronging﴾, meaning renewing the wrong to themselves by placing harm where the gaining of benefit belongs, because they do not take heed by their minds which He set within them so that they might be illumined by them and know truth from falsehood. They do not accept from the guides when they uncover for them what covers those minds, and they do not return from error when the guides press them with the dazzling signs. Rather, they move from heedlessness to obstinacy.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 10:

Since their relapse after these conducive causes was far off, he indicated it with the particle of delay (thumma), or it is an indication of the prolonged duration of the messengers' calling them and their enduring them. So He said: ﴿Then was﴾, that is, it was a state from which there was no escape, and it is at the utmost of horror, as the masculine verb indicates. ﴿The end﴾, that is, the final outcome, ﴿of those who did evil﴾. He placed the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun to generalize and to indicate the cause. ﴿The worst﴾, that is, the condition that is the worst it can be, namely the loss of their souls through destruction in this world and eternal abiding in punishment in the Hereafter, as a recompense to them of the same kind as their deeds. For just as they did evil to the messengers, the King did evil to them. Then he mentioned the reason in His saying: ﴿because they denied﴾, that is, on account of their denying the messengers, treating ﴿the signs of Allah﴾ with contempt, that is, the proofs attributed to the Supreme King, who possesses all perfection, which indicate Him by their greatness according to His greatness, ﴿and they used to﴾, that is, a state as if it were their nature, ﴿mock at them﴾, although they are the furthest thing from mockery, ﴿they used to mock﴾, that is, they persisted in that by renewing it at every moment while magnifying it, to the point that their mockery of anything else was as if it were nonexistent. Just as you yourselves deny what was promised concerning the matter of the Romans and mock at it, so beware lest there befall you what befell the earlier ones, and then you will be returned to Him, glory be to Him, and He will punish you with the greatest punishment. It is also possible that this is a substitute for "the worst" or an explanation of it, in the sense that when they did evil, their evil increased their blindness until they relapsed into blindness, and they arrived at denial and mockery, which is the most evil of conditions, the opposite of what the believer is rewarded with, namely that his faith increases him in guidance.

Since the sum of what has preceded is that He, glory be to Him and exalted, is capable of restoration just as He was capable of origination, and since the affirmation of the self has a state unique to it that belongs to no other, He said, mentioning the outcome of what has preceded and its summary, stating the intended matter explicitly and condensing the proof: ﴿Allah﴾ [i.e., the One encompassing in knowledge and power] ﴿originates creation﴾, i.e., there has come forth from Him what you have seen, and He renews at every moment what He wills of that, as you witness, ﴿then He repeats it﴾ after He annihilates it. He omitted emphasizing it, indicating that He is independent of it, because it is among the accepted premises that whoever brings something into existence is, without doubt, capable of bringing it back.

Since the recompense is a dreadful matter, He indicated it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then to Him﴾ [i.e.] not to other than Him ﴿you will be returned﴾, in meaning in all your affairs in this world, even though you, due to the shortness of your vision, attribute them to causes, and in actuality after the establishment of the Hour. The reading of the majority with the shift to the second person [turja'ūna] is more eloquent, because it is more explicit regarding the intended meaning. Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim and Rawḥ from Yaʿqūb read it with the yāʾ of the third person (yurjaʿūn), in keeping with the preceding pattern.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 12:

Having mentioned the return, he followed it with some of its conditions, saying: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾. It was named so as an indication of the great power over it, together with the multitude of creatures, including those among them who are great, mighty and leaders. ﴿Will be dumbfounded﴾, that is, will fall silent and become still in despair and bewilderment, in utmost humiliation—by what the form of the verb indicates together with renewal and continuity [and persistence]—by what the present tense points to. ﴿The criminals﴾, those who obtained from the world what ought to be cut off because of its perishing, and cut off from the means of the Hereafter what ought to be connected for its enduring. They were at the utmost in confusion in disputation and in knowing everything that enrages the opponent, of speech, action, swaying and laughing mockingly when the opponent falls silent, marvelling at how they run on in their nonsense, and rejoicing at silencing him, so that some of those who see him might suppose that he has been cut off and that the proof is theirs.

Since the silent one may sometimes be sufficed by another's speech, He negated that by His saying, affirming it by making the verb past tense: ﴿And there was not﴾. Since the context calls for belittling them by belittling their partners, He arranged the negation of the painful benefit in this order: ﴿for them﴾. It is also possible that this ordering is meant to restrict the matter, so that the meaning is: ﴿for them﴾, specifically, at that time and not after it, and it was not in the category of that from before, had they been reasoning. As for others, who may rightly be described as criminals because they belong to the people of hidden shirk (ash-shirk al-khafi), some of them may be interceded for by those who raised them, from among the martyrs, the scholars and the believers in general. ﴿From their partners﴾ refers specifically to those they assumed to be partners, so that their confusion and their extreme ignorance in their saying become clear: ﴿These are our intercessors with God﴾ [Yunus: 18]. (p-56) As for others, there occurs from them what is called intercession (ash-shafa'a), sometimes explicitly and sometimes allusively, like the general intercession of our Prophet (ﷺ) for all creation, to decide the judgment. And his (ﷺ) saying concerning certain named people: "My companions, to me, to me!" It is said: "You do not know what they innovated after you." He says: "Away, away!" And the saying of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿And whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [Ibrahim: 36]. ﴿Intercessors﴾ who rescue them from what they are in and what they are facing. Its being expressed in the plural form of multiplicity may be without a restrictive implication, because its context is the rejection of their belief in their earlier saying. It may also be understood that some of those they worshipped may indeed intercede, or allude to intercession, like the saying of Isa, peace be upon him: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 118].

When He mentioned the state of the intercessors with them, He mentioned their state with the intercessors, saying: ﴿And they were﴾, that is, a state of the utmost firmness, ﴿with their partners﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿disbelievers﴾, that is, disowning them, concealing that they had believed them to be gods and had worshipped them, in accordance with their habit regarding what does not benefit them: stubbornness and slander.

[p-57] Since the soul may sometimes long to know whether there will be anything after their despair, He said, informing and terrifying them by repeating what has passed: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, i.e., how awesome is that day! Then He increased its awfulness by saying: ﴿On that day they will be divided﴾, i.e., the believers, who rejoice in God's victory, and the disbelievers will be separated into a division with no reunion after it. These will be in ʿIlliyyīn (the highest station), and those will be in asfala sāfilīn (the lowest of the low).

One of the judges among my companions, may God pardon him, related to me while weeping that he saw a terrifying dream. He saw that the Resurrection had come, and people were being gathered, as described in the hadiths, into one plain, naked, fearful and bewildered, surging over one another. Suddenly a figure of those in authority, with a whip in his hand, drew a line with it on the ground and divided them into two groups. He said: "These are the obedient, and these are the disobedient." He said: "I was among the disobedient." Immediately the obedient disappeared from our sight, and we saw none of them. Then he drew a line again with that whip and divided us into two groups, saying: "These are the disobedient in speech, and these are the disobedient in deeds." He said: "I was among the disobedient in deeds." Then immediately the disobedient in speech disappeared from our sight, and we saw none of them. We remained, some of us sitting and some of us lying down, and we were few compared with the disobedient in speech. While we were in that state, a messenger came to a person beside me, seized him by the heel, then pulled him out, and drew his skin off in one stroke, as if it were a leather bag stripped from something dry. I was seized by intense terror. While I was in that state, another messenger came from behind me, threw over me a woollen cloak (jūkha), placed it over my shoulders, and wrapped it around my thighs, covering me with it, but not in the manner of wearing a sewn garment. He said: "I awoke while still in that condition." I related it to one of the righteous people, and he said: "Praise God that you are among the disobedient in deeds. The manner in which you were covered with the cloak indicates that I will perform Hajj." He gave me this good news, and I performed Hajj that year. God Most High is the One asked for repentance, for He is the Doer of whatever He wills.

﴿As for those who believed﴾, i.e., they affirmed faith with their tongues, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, confirming their affirmation, ﴿the righteous deeds﴾, i.e., all of them.

When the mention of cultivating the earth and making it fit for plants came earlier here, and he admonished those who made it their greatest concern, saying that it would not last for them and did not benefit them at all, He mentioned that He rewards whoever turns away from it in his heart to follow His command, with the greatest of what is seen of its blossoming, its freshness, and its beauty, in a lasting way. So He said: ﴿They, i.e., specifically, are in a garden﴾, i.e., not less than that, [and it is] a very great, wide, spread-out land with abundant water and plants that delight and gladden. This is its original meaning in the language. [And] al-Tabari said: "You will not find a more beautiful sight or a more pleasant fragrance than gardens (riyad)."

﴿They will be made joyful﴾, i.e., they will be gladdened repeatedly, at every time, with a joy by which faces light up, mouths smile, and eyes shine, so that its beauty and radiance appear, and the blessing becomes manifest through the appearance of its effects in the easiest and most agreeable manner.

Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': the original meaning of ḥabra (ḥabrah) in the language is "a trace of beauty." Others said: "ḥabarahu," when it pleases him with a pleasure by which his face lights up and its trace appears in him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 16:

﴿And as for those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., they covered over what the lights of intellects had uncovered,

﴿and denied﴾ out of obstinacy ﴿Our signs﴾, which are no more truthful nor more luminous than their lights, given their greatness with Us, ﴿and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾, which left no ambiguity in its explanation, ﴿those﴾, i.e., the distant and the hateful, ﴿are in punishment﴾, i.e., the complete punishment and nothing else, ﴿brought forth﴾ from whatever place of presentation it may be, by hasty driving and fierce rebuke. When they reach its abode, He appoints over them those who perpetuate their state as such—for the nominal sentence conveys permanence—so they will not be absent from it, nor will it be lightened for them.

When He, glory be to Him, had explained the origin (*mabda'*) through the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the return (*ma'ad*) through Paradise and Hell, and that they denied it, and their denial entailed believing in many deficiencies, among them incapacity, failure to fulfill a promise, and abandonment of wisdom, this was a cause for Him to declare His holy Self free of these and to command that it be declared free. That is because declaring Him free repels from the one who does so the harms of the threat and raises him to the path of the promise. So He said, mentioning from among His lofty acts, of which no one else has any hope of power over any part, what indicates the opposite of that which their belief entails. He turned the speech away from the form of majesty [to something greater than it, by mentioning the greatest Name].

﴿So glory be to God﴾, that is, glorify Him who possesses all majesty, with the comprehensive forms of glorification (*tasbih*), by saying this statement which is His knowledge, so He is free of every deficiency. Then He mentioned the times of glorification, indicating the change that occurs in them, from which He is free, and the renewal of blessings and the occurrence of states within them that indicate the power of origination (*ibda'*), which indicates the resurrection. He said, indicating comprehensiveness by omitting the governing preposition (*naz' al-khafid*), giving precedence to the evening because it is more indicative of the resurrection, which is the point of dispute and the principle, and turning the speech to address (*khitab*) because it is stronger in alerting:

﴿When you enter the evening﴾, that is, at the very beginning of the night's entry, with the removal of the day and the dispersal of its light, whereupon weariness afflicts you and lethargy and idleness penetrate you, in a manner of renewal and continuity. He emphasized the recommendation to glorify by repeating the governing element, saying:

﴿And when you enter the morning﴾, with the transformation of the matter, so that you rise living after you were dead, and you find a day that has shone after a night that was dark. [You then do what He, glory be to Him, is free of, namely movement and striving to bring benefit and to repel harm.] The context guides us to the understanding that the implied meaning is: to Him belongs praise in these two categories.

[p. 60]

When he mentioned what indicates the specific transcendence (tanzih) of God, he followed it with what is known through the general perfection, saying, mentioning the time of the perfection of the day and the perfection of the night, and reminding of what befalls the human being at those two times of deficiency through lethargy and sleep, as an interjection between the times, out of concern to join praise (tahmid) with glorification (tasbih): ﴿And to Him﴾, that is, to Him alone, [together with] freedom from any taint of deficiency, ﴿belongs the praise﴾, that is, the comprehensive ascription of all attributes of perfection.

When He, glory be to Him, had first stated that His transcendence fills the times, and that this necessarily entails filling the created realms, and since affirming perfection is more evidently noble than transcendence above deficiency, He explicitly named both categories, saying: ﴿in the heavens﴾, that is, all the lofty celestial bodies, whose movement, although they are so vast that none but Him, glory be to Him, can encompass them, is a cause of the evening and the morning and of other benefits. ﴿And the earth﴾, in which there are benefits that exceed your comprehension, although in relation to the heaven it is like a ring thrown into a desert. Were it not so, you would have seen that by sighting what lies beyond it, which is the condition of every shade with every small thing, just as you observe clouds and the like.

When He specified the evening and the morning, He generalized, saying, expressing it with what indicates continuity, because the time of sleep, which indicates deficiency, is more deserving of affirming perfection within it: ﴿and in the afternoon﴾, that is, from noon until morning, ﴿and when you enter [the time of] midday﴾, that is, you enter into the intensity of heat. Glory be to God in all of that. So the verse is of the type of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which each of two elements is left implicit where the other is stated): He mentioned glorification first as an indication of its intended sense second, and praise second as an indication of its intended sense first. Perhaps what is meant here by "entering" is more general than the time of midday (zuhr), so that it refers to the period from when the name of morning ceases, at the rising of the sun, until the name of evening arrives, which is from midday to sunset. This was said by Ibn Tarif in his book al-Af'al, and he transmitted it from the imam Abd al-Haqq in his book al-Wa'i. This is the case when the day is at its fullest, so its perfection in what is less than that is a fortiori.

Together with these fine distinctions, this is an allusion to the five daily prayers, that is: glorify Him by submitting to Him through prayer at the time of evening, with the Asr and Maghrib prayers, at the time of morning with the Subh prayer, in the afternoon with the Isha prayer, and at the time of entering [midday] with the Zuhr prayer. In this arrangement there is a fine point showing concern for the middle prayer (al-salat al-wusta). He, glory be to Him, began with Asr, whose identification is the most sound of the opinions, while the inclusion of Maghrib within its scope is by way of following and secondary intention. Then He followed it with Subh, which is next to it in soundness, and these two are the two nearest times, in accordance with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever prays the two cool prayers will enter Paradise," narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him). "Whoever prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will be granted Paradise," which the author of al-Firdaws traced back to Imara ibn Ruwayba (may Allah be pleased with him), and Muslim and others narrated from him with the wording: "No one who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will enter the Fire," meaning Fajr and Asr. "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'Indeed you will see your Lord as you see this moon; you will not be crowded in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do it, do not miss it.'" Then he recited: ﴿And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before the setting﴾ [Qaf 50:39]. Narrated by al-Bukhari from Jarir ibn Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him). The hadith of Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) in the Sahih: "Angels succeed one another among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the Fajr prayer and the Asr prayer," enters here.

He said, having mentioned a sign of the resurrection, which implies the oneness of God, the absolute transformation that is, in meaning, a giving of life after death, he followed it with giving life and causing death in actual reality. He moved from the explicit mention of resurrection to what he had hinted at, and said: ﴿He brings the living out of the dead﴾, like the human and the bird, ﴿from the dead﴾, like the sperm-drop and the egg, ﴿and brings the dead out of the living﴾, the reverse of that, ﴿and revives the earth﴾ by the greening of vegetation.

Since some lands do not grow anything until a period after rain has fallen, while others grow from the moment rain falls, following the destruction of the vegetation that was on them, equally, he dropped the preposition here, drawing attention to the second matter, because it is more indicative of power. It is therefore more fitting to this context and to the purpose of the surah. It also indicates that the strength of its revival is continuous, so he said: ﴿after its death﴾, by its drying and crumbling. Since the implied meaning was: thus He does this repeatedly, and you are watching, he joined to it his saying: (p-64) ﴿And thus﴾, that is, and like His doing this wondrous act of bringing out this living thing, both physically and in meaning, from the dead, ﴿you will be brought out﴾ with the easiest of matters from the earth, after your bodies have scattered into it as dust, which was alive by your life. This is according to the recitation of the majority, which uses the passive voice (al-bina' lil-maf'ul). Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Ibn Dhakwan, with a variant from him, read it in the active voice (al-bina' lil-fa'il), indicating that because of their strong readiness to accept resurrection, they became as though they were coming out by themselves.

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad narrated in the Ziyadat al-Musnad (the additions to the Musnad) from Laqit ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him, that he went out as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him was a companion of his called Nahik ibn Asim ibn Malik ibn al-Muntafiq, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: "So I went out, and my companion, until we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the end of Rajab. We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had finished the morning prayer, and he stood up in the morning delivering a sermon, until he said: '[Indeed] listen, you will live. Indeed, sit. Indeed, sit.' He said: So the people sat, and I and my companion stood [until] when his heart and his sight were free for us, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! What knowledge of the unseen do you have?' He laughed, by the life of Allah, and shook his head, and said: 'Your Lord has withheld the five keys of the unseen,' and he mentioned it until he mentioned the resurrection. He said: I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how will He gather us after the winds, decay and beasts have scattered us?' He said: 'I will inform you of something similar among the signs of Allah: you looked at the earth while it was barren and decayed. I said: It will never live. Then your Lord, mighty and majestic, sent down rain upon it, and it did not remain for you except for a few days until you saw it [upon it] as one single height, and by the life of your God, He is more capable of gathering you from water as He gathers the plants of the earth, and you will come out.'"

Since the sense was: "This is among the signs of God [which] you witness at all times as an indication of your resurrection," He followed it with a reminder of what is more difficult than it in the course of customary events, saying: ﴿And among His signs﴾, i.e., indicating His power to resurrect you. Since the aim was to establish His power, glorified is He, to resurrect them after they had become dust [by His bringing into being their origin from dust], which exceeds resurrection in wonder, in that there was no origin for them in life, and since His doing of that was only once, He spoke in the past tense: ﴿that He created you﴾ through the creation of your father Adam ﴿from dust﴾, which had no origin of attribution to life.

Since the beginning of man from dust is at the extreme of wonder, He pointed to that with the particle of distance, saying: ﴿then﴾, i.e., after bringing you out from it, ﴿when you are human beings﴾ (bashar), i.e., you suddenly find yourselves having a skin (bushra) which is at the extreme of firmness and cohesion together with softness, the reverse of the description you had when you were dust. He attributed the dispersal to the addressed subject rather than to the predicate, because address is more indicative of the intended meaning, so He said: ﴿you disperse﴾, i.e., you reach by dispersal every extent, moving from place to place with reason and speech.

He did not end this verse with what He ended the following with, indicating that it encompasses all the signs and indicates all perfections. And He ended what follows with that, alerting that people neglected to reflect upon them despite their clarity, when it was their duty to place them before their eyes, indicating all that the Books descended with and the Messengers reported. Likewise He emphasized in the report, informing that because of their neglect of them they are in the sphere of denial.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 21:

Since it is more astonishing that He who created them from dust, as males, created from them females, and made the two of them like the sky and the earth in water, vegetation, purity and bounty, He said: ﴿And among His signs﴾, meaning, upon that. Since the creation of a female from a male alone happened only once, like the creation from dust, He expressed it in the past tense and said: ﴿that He created for you﴾, meaning for your sake, so that your kind may endure through procreation. Fronting the prepositional phrase (lakum, "for you") indicates the prohibition of marrying outside your own kind. The expression "from yourselves" (min anfusikum) is clearer in showing that they are from the man's body, in His words: ﴿from yourselves﴾, meaning from your own kind, after their creation from the very being of your father Adam, peace be upon him. ﴿Spouses﴾, meaning females, who are a pair for you ﴿that you may dwell﴾, inclining ﴿towards them﴾ through desire and affection, from the expression "sakana ilayhi" (he found rest in him), when one inclines to a thing, ceases, and feels at peace with it. He did not make them of a kind other than yours, lest you recoil from them.

Since the purpose of dwelling cannot be realized except through the continuance of affection, He said: ﴿And He placed﴾, meaning He made, by means of the creation in this quality, ﴿between you affection﴾ (mawaddah), meaning a meaning among the meanings which requires that neither spouse wish for the other to receive anything they dislike, along with the human nature's inclination to love harm. This is its meaning because the root w-d-d, in both its straight and inverted forms, revolves around expansiveness and emptiness from the desert (dawy) and the desert-like wasteland (dawiyyah), with the waw doubled, which is the wilderness. The words wadd and widad [the lexicon says: love]. Abu 'Abdullah al-Qazzaz said, and Imam 'Abd al-Haqq transmitted it from him in his Wa'i: it is wish (umniyyah). You say, "I wished that such-and-such had been," because of the breadth of the paths of wishes and the branching of the valleys of love. [In al-Qamus]: Wadan is a village near al-Abwa' and a long mountain near Fayd. And al-mawaddah is the writing, because of the breadth of speech in it. Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harali said in his Sharh al-Asma al-Husna: wadd is emptiness [from] the desire for what is disliked. When the desire for good and its preference is attained, it becomes love. Whoever desires only that has indeed shown wadd, and whoever desires good has indeed loved. Wadd is the first step in freeing oneself from the disease of worldly influence, caused by the crowding for it among its seekers of resentment and enmity. That is the manifestation of what is prepared for them of pure love. Thus whoever shows wadd does not sever, and whoever loves connects and prefers. Al-Wadud is the One free from all avenues of evil, outwardly and inwardly.

Since this good meaning is not complete except by the desire for good, He said: ﴿and mercy﴾, meaning [a meaning] that moves each to strive for the other in bringing good and repelling harm. But since the desire for good may come with reproach over something disliked, He combined the two attributes, both of which are from Allah, while the quarrel, which is hatred, is from Satan.

Since that is of such greatness that it is beyond description, He indicated it by His words, emphasizing it in response to their treatment of it by turning away from what it guides them to, the treatment of one who claims that he was left aimless without wisdom. He placed the prepositional phrase first to indicate that its indication is so great that every sign vanishes in its presence, and likewise whatever is of this kind, in the manner of His words:

﴿And We show them no sign but that it is greater than its sister﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 48]. ﴿Indeed in that﴾, meaning that which has preceded of the creation of the spouses in the mentioned state and what follows it of benefits, ﴿are signs﴾, meaning clear indications of the power and wisdom of its Doer.

Since this meaning [together with being] subtle [is grasped through reflection], He said: ﴿for a people﴾, meaning men, or those in their position, who have strength, diligence and vigor in carrying out what is entrusted to them, ﴿who reflect﴾, meaning who employ their thoughts according to the established principles and strive in that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 22:

When He, glorified be He, had mentioned the male and the female, both created from the earth, and the heaven was like the male in relation to the earth from which man was created, and their creation, although they were created from nothing, was more wondrous than His creation of man, and so it is more indicative of power, [and the creation of the earth, which is like the female, preceded the creation of the heaven, contrary to what was the case in man], He followed their mention by beginning with that which is like the male. He said, pointing, after having mentioned the signs within the souls, to the signs of the horizons: ﴿And among His signs﴾, meaning those indicating this, and since it is wondrous that the two horizons were brought into being from non-existence in a continuous, unchanging state, He expressed it by the verbal noun, saying: ﴿the creation of the heavens﴾ in their height and firmness, ﴿and the earth﴾ in its vastness and perfection.

And since there are people who attribute creation to nature (al-tabi'ah), He, exalted be He, mentioned among the attributes of the souls that which nullifies the influence of the horizons by themselves, apart from His creation, His determination, His bringing into being and His management, saying: ﴿and the difference of your tongues﴾, meaning your languages, your tones and their forms, so that you hardly hear two speakers agreeing in whispering or in loudness, in harshness or softness, in stammering or eloquence, in brevity or verbosity, and other attributes of speech and its states, its qualities and its forms, while you are of one soul. If the decision belonged to nature, there would be no difference, because it has no choice, while the relation of all of them to it is one.

And since the color of the sky is one, while the colors of the lands can be counted, He said: ﴿and the difference of your colors﴾, meaning a difference that, despite its variety and closeness, has no fixed limit, while the relation remains one. Were it not for this difference, acquaintance would not occur, benefits would be lost, and advantages would perish. He, glorified be He, omitted the mention of the forms because of the differing forms of the stars through the differences in their shapes, and of the lands through the measures of the mountains and hills and their conditions. So if the difference were due to nature, it would either be with respect to the sky or to the earth. If it were with respect to the sky, its color is one; and if it were with respect to the earth, the color of the people of each region would not be suited to the color of their land. As for tongues, their matter is more evident.

And since this, despite being in the utmost clarity, is not restricted to one kind of creation to the exclusion of others, He said: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, meaning the matter, great and high in rank in its exposition and the manifestation of its proof, ﴿are signs﴾, meaning many indications, very clear, of His oneness, exalted be He, and of His acting by choice, and of the falsity of what the proponents of natures say, of those possibilities which, despite their obscurity, are feeble, and despite their remoteness, are dissolved and dispersed, ﴿for those who know﴾, all of them, not restricted to any one class among them to the exclusion of another, whether jinn, humans, or others. In the reading of Hafs from 'Asim, with the kasra on the lam, it is an urging of the addressees to reflect, so that they may be among the people of knowledge. In the reading of the rest, with the fatha, it is an allusion to the fact that this is so evident that, were inanimate matter to speak, it would report knowledge of it; so in it is an indication that they are as nothing, and there is no rebuke more painful than this.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 23:

When he had mentioned the one who sustains and the one who shades, and those within them, and some of their necessary attributes, he mentioned what arises from each of these of separable attributes, and so he said: ﴿And among His signs﴾, meaning [upon] that and other kinds of power and knowledge, ﴿is your sleep﴾, meaning your sleeping, its place and its time, which overcomes you such that you cannot repel it.

Since the night is the place of rest, tranquility and sleep, he mentioned what He made of sleep during the day as well, because that is more indicative of the act by choice. So he said: ﴿by night and by day﴾, meaning those arising from the heavens and the earth through the difference of movements, which arise only from a free, choosing Agent, and your cutting off, through sleep, from your livelihood [and everything that concerns you], and your rising after your sleep as a compulsory matter over which you have no power to disengage from either of the two at all. ﴿And your seeking﴾, meaning your pursuit with earnestness and effort, ﴿of His bounty﴾ through livelihood in both of them. So the verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device of mutual omission): the mention of sleep indicates rising from it, and the seeking indicates cessation from it; it omitted the end of the first and the beginning of the second. ﴿Surely in that﴾, meaning in the great matter of high rank, from the creation of sleep after vigor, and vigor after sleep, which is the lesser death, and the creation of each of the two (night and day) after their annihilation, and the earnestness in seeking together with the variation in attainment, ﴿are signs﴾, meaning numerous ones, indicating power and wisdom, especially the resurrection.

Since these signs, in their indication of what they point to, namely the resurrection and action by choice, are subtle, the intellect cannot stand independently in grasping them without instruction from the callers (to truth), because sleep and seeking may be ascribed to servants, and none goes beyond that to the Creator except the select few of sincere servants. The sleeper rises clear-minded, with an empty heart and an active body. He said: ﴿for a people who hear﴾, meaning from the sincere callers, the hearing of one who has awoken from his sleep, whose body is rested and vigorous and whose heart is free from anything that clouds advice or prevents its acceptance; or the meaning is: for a people who are fit to hear, having awoken from their slumber and so turned back from their obstinacy, indicating that whoever does not reflect upon these signs is asleep, not awake, and so is not qualified to hear.

ولَمّا خَتَمَ بِالسَّمْعِ آيَةً جَمَعَتْ آياتِ الأنْفُسِ والآفاقِ لِكَوْنِها [نَشَأتْ مِن أحْوالِ البَشَرِ والخافِقَيْنِ، افْتَتَحَ بِالرُّؤْيَةِ آيَةً أُخْرى جامِعَةً لَهُما لِكَوْنِها ناشِئَةً عَنْهُما مَعَ كَوْنِها] أدُلَّ عَلى المَقْصُودِ جامِعَةً بَيْنَ (p-73) التَّرْغِيبِ والتَّرْهِيبِ فَقالَ: ﴿ومِن آياتِهِ﴾ [And among His signs]. ولَمّا كانَ لَمَعانُ البَرْقِ جَدِيرًا بِالتِماعِ البَصَرِ [عِنْدَ] أوَّلِ رُؤْيَةٍ، وكانَ يَتَجَدَّدُ في حِينٍ دُونَ حِينٍ، عَبَّرَ بِالمُضارِعِ (al-mudari', the present tense) حاذِفًا الدّالَّ عَلى إرادَةِ المَصْدَرِ (al-masdar, the verbal noun) لِلدَّلالَةِ عَلى التَّجَدُّدِ المُعْجِبِ مِنهُ فَقالَ: ﴿يُرِيكُمُ البَرْقَ﴾ [He shows you the lightning], أيْ عَلى هَيْئاتٍ وكَيْفِيّاتٍ طالَما شاهَدْتُمُوها تارَةً تَأْتِي بِما يَضُرُّ وتارَةً بِما يَسُرُّ، ولِذَلِكَ قالَ مُعَبِّرًا بِغايَةِ الإخافَةِ والإطْماعِ لِأنَّ الغاياتِ هي المَقْصُودَةُ بِالذّاتِ: ﴿خَوْفًا﴾ [as a fear], أيْ لِلْإخافَةِ مِنَ الصَّواعِقِ المُحْرِقَةِ ﴿وطَمَعًا﴾ [and as a hope], أيْ ولِلْطَماعِ في المِياهِ الغَدِقَةِ، وعَبَّرَ بِالطَّمَعِ لِعَدَمِ الأسْبابِ المُوصِلَةِ إلَيْهِ.

ولَمّا كانَ البَرْقُ غالِبًا مِنَ المُبَشِّراتِ بِالمَطَرِ، وكانَ ما يَنْشَأُ عَنِ الماءِ أدَلَّ شَيْءٍ عَلى البَعْثِ، أتْبَعَهُ شَرْحَ ما أشارَ إلَيْهِ بِهِ مِنَ الطَّمَعِ فَقالَ: ﴿ويُنَـزِّلُ﴾ [and He sends down], ولَمّا كانَ إمْساكُ الماءِ في جِهَةِ العُلُوِّ في غايَةِ الغَرابَةِ، قالَ مُحَقِّقًا لِلْمُرادِ بِالإنْزالِ مِنَ المَوْضِعِ الَّذِي لا يُمْكِنُ لِأحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ دَعْواهُ ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً﴾ [water from the sky].

ولَمّا جَعَلَ سُبْحانَهُ ذَلِكَ سَبَبًا لِتَعَقُّبِ الحَياةِ قالَ: ﴿فَيُحْيِي بِهِ﴾ [and thereby gives life], أيِ الماءَ النّازِلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ خاصَّةً لِأنَّ أكْثَرَ الأرْضِ لا تُسْقى بِغَيْرِهِ ﴿الأرْضَ﴾ [the earth], أيْ بِالنَّباتِ الَّذِي هو لَها كالرُّوحِ لِجَسَدِ الإنْسانِ، ولَمّا كانَتِ الأرْضُ لَيْسَ لَها مِن ذاتِها في الإنْباتِ إلّا العَدَمُ، وكانَ إحْياؤُها (p-74) بِهِ مُتَكَرِّرًا، فَكانَ كَأنَّهُ دائِمٌ، [وكانَ ذَلِكَ أنْسَبَ لِمَقْصُودِ السُّورَةِ] حَذَفَ الجارَّ قائِلًا: ﴿بَعْدَ مَوْتِها﴾ [after its death], أيْ بِيُبْسِهِ وتَهَشُّمِهِ ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ﴾ [Indeed, in that], [أيْ] الأمْرِ العَظِيمِ العالِي القَدْرِ ﴿لآياتٍ﴾ [are signs], لا سِيَّما عَلى القُدْرَةِ عَلى البَعْثِ. ولَمّا كانَ ذَلِكَ ظاهِرًا كَوْنُهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ الفاعِلِ بِالِاخْتِيارِ لِوُقُوعِهِ في سَحابٍ دُونَ سَحابٍ وفي وقْتٍ دُونَ آخَرَ وفي بَلَدٍ دُونَ آخَرَ، وعَلى هَيْئاتٍ مِنَ القُوَّةِ والضَّعْفِ والبَرْدِ والحَرِّ وغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الأمْرِ، وكانَ مِنَ الوُضُوحِ في الدَّلالَةِ عَلى البَعْثِ بِمَكانٍ لا يَخْفى عَلى عاقِلٍ قالَ: ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [for a people who reason].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 25:

When all of the preceding visible signs (al-ayat al-mar'iyyat) originated from these two great creations, which encompass those to whom these audible signs (al-ayat al-masmu'at) were revealed, serving as an explanation for whoever found the matter of the visible signs unclear, He mentioned a matter comprehensive of all of them, and it is so evident that it needs no more than the intellect which the preceding was sealed with, so He said: ﴿And among His signs﴾, meaning, [signs] of complete power and perfect wisdom.

Since this verse concerns permanence (al-thubat) and not renewal (al-tajaddud), He brought the particle that indicates the mutability of the verb (al-harf al-dall 'ala al-masrif), in order to strip the verb of the future tense (li-yaslakha al-fi'l 'an al-istiqbal), and He expressed it with the present tense, because it is necessary to remove the two from this state. So He said: ﴿that the heaven and the earth stand﴾, meaning, remain upon what you witness of this great matter without a pillar, ﴿the heaven﴾, [which He] made singular because the first heaven (al-sama' al-ula) (p-75) does not admit dispute, since it is observed, together with the word's suitability for all [heavens], since it is a collective noun (jins). ﴿And the earth﴾, despite their heaviness and weight which necessitate falling, ﴿by His command﴾, not by anything other than Him.

Since no doubt remained in His perfect knowledge and complete power, He said, expressing with the particle of delay (adat al-tarakhi) so that it indicates, together with its own meaning, magnificence: and He said, indicating that His power over all things is equal despite their distance, and that there is no difference in Him regarding the comprehensiveness of His command between the standing of living beings and the standing of the earth and heaven: ﴿Then, when He calls you﴾, and He pointed to the insignificance of that matter to Him by His saying: ﴿with one call from the earth﴾, despite the distance between it and the heaven, let alone the Throne, and He emphasized that by it being like the blink of an eye or even closer, so He said, expressing with the particle of suddenness (adat al-fuja'a): ﴿behold, you come forth﴾, meaning, this attribute renews for you after your dissolution through death and decay, and it recurs with regard to each of you without any delay or respite at all, except that it may be ordered from the most excellent to the most excellent, in accordance with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I am the first whom the earth will split open for," as He called you from it first when He created you from dust, then, when you are human beings dispersing (bashar tantashirun). And He left this [verse] free of what concluded the preceding verses, as an alert that it is like the first [sign] which has reached the peak of manifestness, especially with its joining to the first, which is the greatest indicator of them, to a degree that is brighter than light, as its reference will come in the verse "And it is easier for Him."

(p-76) When He had mentioned His disposal of the container and some of what is contained in it, of mankind and jinn, He mentioned His subjugation of all of them, saying: ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, [He alone] with the most complete ownership, ﴿whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, all of them. He indicated ownership by His saying: ﴿All are to Him devoutly obedient﴾, that is, He alone. Since the submission of the group necessitates the submission of the individual, but not vice versa, He used the plural in His saying ﴿devoutly obedient﴾ (qanitun), that is, sincere in submission, having in reality and fact no disposal in any way at all, for themselves or for anyone other than Him, except by His permission. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Obedient in the obedience of will, even if they disobey His command in worship." Al-Baghawi and others related it from him, and al-Tabari preferred it. This is the meaning of what I have said.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 27:

When this is a meaning that everyone witnesses within himself, together with what He, glory be to Him, has displayed of the wondrous signs that have passed, and the matter has become so clear to a great degree, He said: ﴿And He is the One who begins the creation﴾, that is, not other than Him, ﴿then He repeats it﴾, that is, by way of renewal, as you witness; and He indicated the magnitude of the return by the particle of delay (thumma), so He said: ﴿then He repeats it﴾, that is, after He annihilates it.

Since it is among what is inherent in the natural disposition (fitra) of all human beings that the repetition of a thing is easier than its initiation, He said: ﴿And it is easier for Him﴾, that is, that return which they deny is easier for Him, addressing them in terms of what they are accustomed to and understand. For this reason He postponed the relative clause (ṣila), because there is no meaning here for the exclusivity (ikhtiṣāṣ) which its fronting (taqdīm) conveys.

Since this is an illustration (tamthīl) for what is hidden from them by means of what is evident to them, and each of the two matters, in relation to His power, is on an equal footing (there is nothing in His knowledge more manifest than another, nor in His power is one more fitting than the other), He said, pointing to the declaring of His holy self free from what some fools may imagine of that: ﴿And to Him belongs the highest description﴾, that is, to Him alone, ﴿the highest description﴾, that is, He who is transcendent above every trace of deficiency and has seized every rank of perfection, and it is His command which encompasses every possible thing, so that by it His own encompassing of every known thing is understood, glory be to Him, as was mentioned earlier in al-Baqara in the explanation of "mathal" (example).

﴿Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54].

Since creation, because of their deficiency, is restricted to what they have some kind of witnessing of, He said: ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾, which He created and which did not resist Him. How then could anything in them resist Him? They have said that the intended meaning of "mathal" here is "attribute" (ṣifa). In my view, it may be on its literal meaning, bringing it near to our intellects. So when we wish to know Him, glory be to Him, in the matter of dominion, we give an example from the highest of what we know of our kings, and we say: "Istiwa' upon the throne" is an example for administration and sole possession of dominion, just as it is said of our kings: "So-and-so sat upon the throne of sovereignty," meaning: he became independent in command and sole in administration, even if there is no throne here and no sitting. And when His seizing and His taking of His enemies is mentioned, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The hand of Allah is above their hands﴾ [al-Fath: 10], ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ [al-Buruj: 12], we give an example of it by what a ruler would do if he subdued his enemies by his firmness, the soundness of his administration and the multitude of his soldiers, so we say: "His sword destroyed his enemies," and we apply the word "sword" to the aforementioned strength. And when it is said: "They run before Our eyes" (tajri bi-a'yunina) and the like, we know that it is like what we say when we see a king of good administration who does not neglect anything of the affairs of his subjects, so we say: "He is in utmost wakefulness," and we apply "wakefulness," which is the opposite of sleep, to good observation, great administration and comprehensive knowledge. These are details of what I stated to be its like, namely His encompassing command, through which the unseen of His holy essence, glory be to Him, has become manifest to us. Likewise, what comes of such examples: we take the spirit of the expression from it, and we know that this is what is intended, and that this apparent wording was mentioned only to bring it near to minds that are deficient, according to what we know of the highest of examples. The matter beyond that is higher than what we know. For this reason, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, that is, alone, the One who, when He wills something, it is in utmost submission to Him, whatever it may be; ﴿the Wise﴾, that is, the One who, when He wills something, perfects it, so that no other can reach any diminishing of it. The wisdom of this existence cannot be complete in this form except by the Resurrection; rather it is the greatest locus of wisdom, so that every possessor of a right reaches his right with the most complete freedom, as we understand it; otherwise falsehood would have more right than truth and would be greater, and so the non-existence of this existent would be better than its existence and more judicious.

When it became clear from this that He alone is the sole possessor of dominion, with comprehensive knowledge, perfect power, and complete wisdom, His saying was linked to the excellence of His parables and the soundness of His speech and deeds: ﴿He has set forth for you﴾, that is, by His wisdom, concerning the matter of the idols, and to demonstrate the invalidity of those who associate partners with Him and the corruption of their claim, by the clearest possible establishment of proof, ﴿a parable﴾ beginning ﴿from yourselves﴾, which are the nearest things to you. You are therefore most fit to understand what you are being reminded of.

Since the essential point of the parable is that a slave cannot be a partner to his master, and since the establishment of proof is closer to reminding and further from repulsion, He said, rebuking, censuring, and establishing the matter: ﴿Do you have﴾, that is, O you who worship alongside Allah some of His servants, ﴿from among what your right hands possess﴾, that is, from among the slaves or maidservants who are human beings like you, ﴿any﴾. The negation, which is what is intended by the interrogative, is generalized by the addition of the preposition in His saying ﴿partners﴾, that is, in any state of affairs by which it would be permissible for you to make partners for Allah. He draws attention to what is involved in the creation of provision, then its distribution among creatures, and other of His affairs, by His saying, as an iltifat (a shift from the third person to the first person), after a long expression in the third person, which might give the impression of distance, to the first person plural, which indicates, along with nearness, majesty and the pleasure of direct address: (p-80) ﴿in what We have provided you﴾, that is, by virtue of Our majesty, of wealth or standing, while your own possession of it is weak.

Since partnership causes the two partners to be equal in the shared matter, He said: ﴿so you﴾, that is, you company of free men and slaves. Since it might be thought that "from partners" is a description of children from their concubines, He placed the prepositional phrase first to prevent this, saying: ﴿therein﴾, that is, in that thing in which the partnership occurs, from that provision specifically and not something else, such as lineage, ancestry, or the like, [or lightness of body or heart, or length of life, or the like. As for their children by concubines, they may be equal to them in these and in other matters of lineage and the like, and slaves may equal them in bodily strength and length of life, or even surpass them], ﴿equal﴾. Then He clarified the equality, which is that the ruling concerning one of the two groups in the shared matter is on a par with the ruling concerning the other, so that neither of them has independent authority over anything, by His saying: ﴿you fear them﴾, that is, O company of masters, regarding disposal of that shared thing.

[Since the particle of comparison is more explicit, he affirmed it and said]: ﴿as you fear one another﴾, that is, as you fear some of those whom you make partners with you, those who are equal to you in freedom and dignity, that they might dispose of the shared matter in a way that does not satisfy them and without their permission. Thus it became clear that your situation with your slaves is an example [for it] concerning those whom you have made partners with Him, clarifying its invalidity. If you do not accept this for yourselves, namely that your slaves be equal to you in (p-81) ownership, how then do you accept it with your Creator regarding these partners you have claimed, making them equal to Him, when they are among the weakest of His creatures? ﴿Do you not then feel shame?﴾

Since this example is at the peak of perfection, the listener would be inclined to say: "Glory be to Allah! How exalted is the rank of this exposition! Does He explain everything in this way?" So He said: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like this lofty exposition, ﴿We detail﴾, that is, We explain, because detailing (fasl) is distinguishing and clarifying, and this is in a magnificent manner, as indicated by the intensive form together with renewal and continuity: ﴿the signs﴾, that is, the clear proofs.

Since clarification does not benefit one who has been deprived of reason, He said: ﴿for a people who reason﴾, indicating that if they do not act in accordance with this, they are madmen, because the parable reveals the meanings through depiction and formation, revealing them in a manner that leaves no ambiguity. Whoever fails to grasp it has no discernment.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 29:

When their answer was decisively, "We have no partners of this description," the implied meaning is: "You have not followed any evidence in associating others with God." So ﴿Bal﴾ ("Rather") is coordinated with it. The original wording would have been "you followed" (ittaba'tum), but he turned away from them, indicating that the anger is at its extreme because of obstinacy after clarification, and he made manifest the attribute that moved them to that, [generalizing and attaching the judgment to it], and said: ﴿followed﴾ [i.e., by burdening themselves against the original disposition] ﴿those who did wrong﴾, meaning they placed a thing in other than its place, like the act of one walking in darkness, ﴿their desires﴾, which is what their souls incline toward.

Since following desire may coincide with evidence, and when it does not, and the one who has knowledge is turned back by his knowledge, he said: ﴿without knowledge﴾, as an indication of how far they are in error, because the ignorant person wanders aimlessly with no preponderant factor other than inclination, like a beast that nothing turns back; whereas the one with knowledge is perhaps turned back by his knowledge.

Since this might lead some to the illusion that this changes His, glorified be He, will, he indicated by the fa' of causation that the implied meaning is: "And this is their error by the will of God, [so when they went to extremes in it, their end was evil and abandonment, because they removed themselves far from the means of guidance]": ﴿So who can guide﴾, meaning without the will of God, and he turned the discourse from the manifestation of majesty to something greater than it, by mentioning the Greatest Name, as the situation required, and said: ﴿whom God has led astray﴾, He to whom the whole affair belongs. By the conjunctive waw he indicated that the implied meaning is: no one guides them [because they removed themselves far from the means of guidance, so they were distanced from the means of victory, since they had come to be on a crumbling precipice in all their affairs; therefore the placement of his following it with the words]: ﴿And they have no﴾, and he intensified the negation, saying: ﴿helpers﴾, meaning neither idols nor others will deliver them from what they are in of abandonment and the captivity of Satan, and from what it causes of fires. He negated all of them rather than one, because reason is a helper for them through the understanding it is equipped with and through following the evidence of revelation, if they had used it; or because it came as an answer to the like of "They have taken gods besides God that they may be a might for them. No! They will deny their worship of them" [or to indicate that following desire does not benefit in remedying its matter except with many helpers]. He indicated the negation of the one by ﴿No soul will avail for another soul﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 48], the verse, and ﴿And that the disbelievers have no protector﴾ [Muhammad: 11], [and] ﴿So he will have no power nor any helper﴾ [At-Tariq: 10], and similar verses.

(p. 84) When the proofs had been clearly established, the signposts erected, the hidden matters made plain, the allusions made explicit, and the tongues of expression made eloquent, He turned to the essence of creation, giving notice that no one else understands this in its true understanding. So He said, as a consequence of that and as an illustration of his turning, uprightness, and steadfastness: ﴿So set your face⁠—that is, your whole intent⁠—toward the religion﴾, meaning, firmly fixed, such that you are absent from anything other than it. Do not turn away from it at all, and do not cease to be watchful. For whoever is concerned with something directs his gaze toward it and straightens his face for it.

Then he alluded to the coarseness of the people of misguidance, their veiling, their density and dullness, their rigidity and hardness, by saying: ﴿hanifan⁠—that is, while you are inclining toward the proof, gentle and pliant, of penetrating patience, of bright insight, of far-reaching thought, quick to transition, swift in thought.

(p. 85) Then he made clear that this disposition is in the nature of every person, although they vary in it. As you see, when they are children they are the easiest thing to lead. But when circumstances reveal to them, in many matters, that their submission was an error, they begin to train themselves in opposition constantly, until it becomes for some of them a habit acquired by practice. So the one who was the easiest and most compliant becomes the hardest and most rigid. This is most common among bad companions who say what they do not do. For this reason he forbade that a child be promised something that has no reality. Ahmad and Ibn Abi al-Dunya related through al-Zuhri, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), (al-Mundhiri said: he did not hear it from him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says to a child, 'Come, take this!' and then does not give it to him, it is a lie." And Abu Dawud, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from the mawla of Abdullah ibn Amir (Ibn Abi al-Dunya's version says: Ziyad: "from Abdullah ibn Amir") that his mother (may Allah be pleased with her) said to him, "Come, I will give you something." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "What did you intend to give him?" She said: "Dates." He said: "As for you, if you had not given him anything, a lie would have been written against you."

Then he said, making clear to them the soundness of his religion by a matter that is in their own selves, just as he made clear the falsity of their religion by a matter that is in their own selves: ﴿the nature of Allah﴾, that is, adhere to the natural disposition of the King to whose command none can repel, which is the original creation upon which He created mankind, and the first nature. [Al-Ghazali said at the end of the Book of Knowledge of the Ihya' (Revival of the Religious Sciences), in explaining the intellect regarding this verse: that is, every human being is created upon belief in Allah the Exalted, indeed upon knowledge of things as they are, meaning that they are as if included in him by the closeness of his readiness for perception. End.] Then he emphasized this by saying: ﴿upon which He created mankind﴾, that is, everyone who has the capacity for movement, ﴿upon it﴾, all of them, the wretched and the blessed. It is the ease of submission and the nobility of character, which in form is the natural disposition of Islam. The verification of this is that what is observed in all children is soundness of natures and smoothness of submission [to the apparent proof]. Among them there is no difficulty in this, as there is with adults, even if they differ in it. So the intended meaning of the natural disposition is their acceptance of the truth and their capacity to comprehend it, just as you find a mute person comprehending the matter of the Return with clear comprehension, having a firmly established faculty in it. This is the meaning indicated by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) in the two Sahihs, and the hadith of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) in Ahmad ibn Mani', that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: (p. 86) "Every newborn is born upon the natural disposition." And in a narration of al-Bukhari: "No newborn is born except upon the natural disposition. Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see in it any mutilated? Until you yourselves mutilate it." Therefore, the cutting of ears, branding, slitting of ears, and the like are an example of the characteristics that the child learns from those who deal with him in them, such as deceit, lying, and other things. Likewise is the hadith of Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi (may Allah be pleased with him) in Muslim, concerning the description of the Fire, and in al-Nasa'i's Fada'il al-Qur'an, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every property I have bestowed upon a servant is lawful, and indeed I created My servants as ḥunafa' (upright monotheists), all of them. Then the devils came to them, led them astray from their religion, made unlawful for them what I had made lawful, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for."

But the devil does not gain power except by Allah's empowering him in the present state, through what He creates in the inner being of the forsaken, of inclination, and in the past through the natures with which He prepared him for such things. This is indicated by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), agreed upon in the Sahih, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "Act, for each is facilitated for what he was created for." And the verse of Surat Subhan (al-Isra): ﴿Each acts according to his own manner﴾ [al-Isra: 84]. That is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) informed them that Allah the Exalted had decreed the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, so that nothing is added to them or subtracted from them, they said: "Shall we not rely upon our decree and abandon action?" So the decree is a proof against them, because its basis is that so-and-so is among the people of the Fire because he did not do such and such. They wanted to make it a proof for themselves. Know that in this there are two matters, neither of which invalidates the other: an inner matter, which is the cause that necessitates in the ruling of lordship, and it is knowledge; and an outer matter, which is the mark that is binding in the right of servanthood, and it is action. The latter is a sign of imagination that does not establish the reality of knowledge. They were made aware of this so that their fear would be attached to the hidden inner matter, which is concealed from them, and their hope to the outer matter, which is manifest to them. Fear and hope are the two stages of servanthood, so that by this they may complete the attribute of faith. The parallel to this is two matters: the provision that is apportioned together with the command to earn, and the appointed term that is fixed together with treatment by medicine. The hidden in these two is the necessitating cause, and the outer is an imagined means. The elite and the common among them have agreed that the outer of these two is not abandoned because of the inner. Al-Razi mentioned its meaning in al-Lawami', from al-Khattabi.

Since the soundness of the original natural disposition is a continuing matter, He said: ﴿There is no alteration﴾ (p. 88) And because of the greatness of the station, He repeated the greatest Name, saying: ﴿in the creation of Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, to whom there is no equal. No one can make a child at the beginning of his life of corrupt disposition, one who does not submit to what is led to him, nor surrender to the one who raises him. Whenever he grows up and advances in years, he returns to what he was formed upon, of disbelief or belief, of obedience or disobedience, of denial or recognition, little by little, until he is drawn to that at puberty or after it. If he dies before that, he is recompensed according to what Allah knew of him, that he would do it naturally and die upon it, like the boy whom al-Khidr (peace be upon him) killed. The report is sound that he was formed upon disbelief. He is not punished for what would be accidental from him, while He knows that it would occur if he had lived, like the parents of the boy, since it was stated explicitly that if he had lived he would have overwhelmed them with transgression and disbelief. So He knew from them disbelief at that time, yet they were not held accountable for it, because it was accidental and not natural. So the consideration is at death, and whoever is formed upon something does not die upon something else. So verify this and you will know that there is no contradiction between any of the texts, neither from the Book nor from the Sunnah. And Allah is the Guide.

Since inclining toward the proof, however it inclines, is a matter whose extent cannot be fully grasped and which is not attained except by the success granted by Allah, He indicated its greatness by saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, the great matter, which is being moved by the proof and following what it points to and urges (p. 89) ﴿is the upright religion﴾, in which there is no crookedness. ﴿But most people﴾ have trained themselves in following desires, because of the doubts that preceded, so that they have come to the state where ﴿they do not know﴾, that is, they have no knowledge at all by which they could distinguish truth from falsehood, because of the harshness that has overcome them.

When some of the people were blessed by God by being in this arena, and their aspiration soared to compete with the horsemen, then when they saw that He had not turned to them and had not relied on them at all, their souls nearly took flight. It was the custom of the people to address the people in order to address their leader, honouring him and urging them to adorn themselves with what he was singled out for. Their hearts were consoled and their breasts expanded, so the state (*hal*, a circumstantial clause) was made clear to them from the pronoun in ”أقِمْ“ (*aqim*, "establish"), or from the governing element in ”فِطْرَتَ“ (*fitrata*, "the natural disposition"). This announced that they were the intended addressees of the discourse and were pointed to as the right ones. So He said: ﴿turning back (to Him)﴾, that is, returning again and again, by the pull of the soul against the original disposition, ﴿to Him﴾, the Exalted, by withdrawing from the bad morals you have acquired and returning to that sound disposition, which submits to proof and inclines to the straight path.

Since, after returning to the clear road, nothing remains but the command to hold fast to it, out of fear of straying from it, as in the first instance, He said, connecting by conjunction to ﴿So establish [the religion]﴾ [al-Rum: 30]: ﴿And fear Him﴾, that is, be afraid lest you deviate from His path, lest He deliver you into the hands of those misguiding ones. When you fear Him and hold fast to it, you will be among those who have emptied themselves of vices ﴿and establish the prayer﴾, so that you become among those who have adorned themselves with virtues. Thus is the way of the religion always: emptying, then adorning. The first entry into Islam is purification (*tanzih*), and the first entry into the Qur'an is seeking refuge (*isti'adhah*). This is an evident, rational matter. Its example is one who wants to write on something: if he first wipes away what is written on it, he benefits from what he writes; otherwise he spoils the first and does not get to read the second. And God is the Granter of success.

Since shirk is among the greatest evils, a place that no other evil shares, He emphasized the prohibition against it by His saying: ﴿And do not be﴾, that is, in any state, ﴿among the polytheists﴾. That is, do not be among those who are counted in their number through friendship, companionship, or any action in which you resemble them. For ("Whoever imitates a people is one of them"). This is general to every kind of shirk, whether it is the worship of an idol, of fire, or of other things, or the practice of a religion that contradicts the texts, such as the sayings of rabbis and monks, and other things besides.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 32:

Since they thought that they were upon the right course, he set up for them a proof of its falsehood through something clearer than it, which no one can hesitate about. That is because it is impossible for a thing to be characterized by the negation of something and its affirmation at one and the same time. So He said, in apposition: ﴿Of those who split up﴾ when they departed from ﴿their religion﴾, which is the original natural disposition (al-fitrah al-ula), so that every people among them worshipped something and adopted a religion different from the religion of those other than them. This is the meaning of ﴿and became sects﴾, i.e., by their effort and diligence in that departure which divided them, ﴿sects﴾, meaning factions allied with one another, each one of them supporting those who follow its religion against those who oppose them, until some of them declared others to be unbelievers and considered their blood and property lawful. Thus it is known with certainty that they are not all upon the truth.

Since this is a matter that is astonishing in its occurrence, he increased its strangeness by saying, as a resumption: ﴿Every faction﴾, i.e., of them, ﴿rejoices in what is with them﴾, i.e., in the particular part of the misguidance they have adopted that is most special to them, ﴿rejoicing﴾, supposing that they have hit upon the truth and attained it to the exclusion of others.

When this became clear to every intelligent person, namely that most of creation is astray, and the situation called for asking about the way out of this error, it was indicated that the way out is adhering to collective unity (al-ijtima'). This was explained in a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya) from the subject of "exultant" (farihun), where He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when﴾. The original would have been "touched them", but it was said [as "touched mankind"] because it is more suitable to the purpose of the surah than restricting this to humans, as is the custom in most surahs, or for other reasons related to the kinds of the world, ﴿touches mankind﴾, to strengthen the intention of generality [indicating every being that has the capacity for swaying, which is movement, from the dumb animals and the inanimate objects. Were they to speak and then move, they would turn toward Him, glorified is He, and would not deviate from Him, just as they are now, in the tongues of their states. This is the consensus (al-ijma') in which no dispute can be conceived.] (p-92) ﴿a harm, they call upon their Lord﴾, meaning the One who has no partner in bestowing benevolence upon them [throughout the whole duration of their being touched by that harm, as indicated by the adverbial expression], while they are ﴿turning back﴾, that is, returning from all their errors that had separated them from Him, ﴿to Him﴾ [Ar-Rum: 31], knowing that there is no relief for them with anything other than Him. This is the custom of all of them; none of them deviates from it at any time or in any crisis. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami' at the end of al-'Ankabut: "This is evidence that the knowledge of the Lord is in the innate nature of every human being, and that if they are heedless in times of ease, there is no doubt that they take refuge in Him in times of hardship."

Since everyone in hardship regards deliverance from it as extremely unlikely, He said: ﴿then﴾, with the particle of distance, ﴿when He makes them taste﴾ [attributing mercy to Himself out of reverence for good manners, although all of it is from Him]. Since the whole context concerns tawhid, the attention to invoking the worshipped One by His name and pronoun was more complete, so He said: ﴿from Him﴾, placing His pronoun first, indicating by fronting the prepositional phrase exclusivity and that no one other than Him is able to do that. He said: ﴿mercy﴾, that is, deliverance from that harm, indicating that if He were to seize them for their sins, He would destroy them; there is no cause for His bounty except His generosity. It also showed how quickly they hasten to deny the favor by His words, expressing it with the particle of suddenness: ﴿then, when a faction of them﴾, that is, a group deserving of separation from the truth, ﴿with their Lord﴾, that is, the One who always does good to them, renewing this bounty for them after this harm, ﴿associate partners﴾ instead of what was incumbent upon them, namely that they should give thanks. Thus it is known that the truth from which there is no deviation is turning back to Him in every state, just as they unanimously did at the time of calamities. Anything other than this that has divided them is error, which cannot be counted as equal to Him, nor can anything be deemed His equal.

When this act is one that only someone extremely foolish or obstinate would commit, and they claimed to be the most intelligent of people, He raised them above the level of the simple-minded to a level where madness would be better than it, mocking them. So He said: ﴿so that they may disbelieve in what We have given them﴾. He turned the speech to the manifestation of greatness and said: ﴿We have given them﴾, meaning of the mercy whose greatness is that none other than Us can grant it, as a safeguard against their falling into another hardship, whereby We would destroy them for what they have angered Us with, or as a means of seeking, through that, to rescue them whenever they fall into the like of it. How misguided their minds are and how foolish their opinions!
