When their action was a cause of the utmost anger, He indicated this through His threat, turning to address them directly with His saying: ﴿So enjoy yourselves﴾, meaning with what you desire in associating partners with Him, through your gathering at the idols, your connection with them, and your mutual affection. He made the consequence of this enjoyment His saying: ﴿for you will come to know﴾, meaning there will be for you, by a promise that admits no breaking, knowledge, so you will recognize when calamity befalls you and the disliked thing encompasses you all, whether any of the idols will benefit you, or those whom you took as a favor-holder by worshipping them and agreeing with him in drawing near to them. (p-94)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 35:

When He rebuked them with His saying: ﴿Do you have any of what your right hands possess as partners in what We have provided you?﴾ [al-Rum: 28], and what preceded it was connected to it as being in the utmost degree of connection, He turned back to them, shifting (iltifat) to the third-person form (maqam al-ghaybah) as a notice of their insignificance, in order to distance them from His presence, since He had made these proofs manifest to them and they persisted in the danger of provoking His anger, with His saying: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority﴾ by what We have of greatness, ﴿clear, compelling proof﴾, that is, a clear and overpowering proof, ﴿so it﴾, that is, that authority, due to the manifestness of its clarity, ﴿speaks﴾ with a figurative speech through its indication and its making things understood, and it bears witness ﴿to what﴾, that is, to the soundness of that which ﴿they were﴾, that is, in firmly established state, ﴿by it﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿associating partners﴾, to such an extent that they found no alternative but to follow it, so that blame would be removed from them. This phrasing indicates that they were so constantly attached to shirk that it became for them a disposition that could not be separated from them.

When these two equal matters made clear that their own customary disposition did not compel them to associate partners with God, that is, no constant, ever-present custom in themselves, no manifest rational proof, and no compelling command from God, it became evident that they follow neither reason nor transmitted authority. Rather, they are captives of desire, founded on sheer ignorance. He had stated this explicitly after the first equivalent, and here he alluded to it, leaving out an explicit statement because the first was sufficient. He argued for it with evidence that they contravened, both the constant habit and the settled evidence of direct observation. So he said, joining by the conjunction ﴿وإذا مَسَّ﴾ [al-Rum: 33] and indicating the lightness of their judgment from another aspect than the first: ﴿وإذا﴾ expressing, with the particle of certainty, an indication that mercy is more abundant than retribution (p-95). He attributed the verb to Himself in the station of majesty, indicating the vastness of His bounty, and said: ﴿أذَقْنا﴾ [and the discourse proceeded in the general pattern of the past tense, in keeping with the purpose of the surah, that the whole matter belongs to Him in everything, so He said]: ﴿النّاسَ رَحْمَةً﴾, that is, a blessing such as wealth or the like, having no cause except Our mercy, ﴿فَرِحُوا بِها﴾, that is, they rejoiced with the rejoicing of those who are secure, insolent, and confident of its non-cessation, forgetting the gratitude of the One who bestowed it. He said: ﴿وإنْ﴾ with the particle of doubt, indicating that calamities are fewer in occurrence, and he said: ﴿تُصِبْهُمْ﴾ without attributing it to Himself, as a lesson to His servants and an announcement of His abundant generosity, ﴿سَيِّئَةٌ﴾, that is, a hardship that distresses them, such as drought or the like.

Since calamities are caused by sins, he said, alerting them to this and denouncing their despair while they do not turn back from the sins for which they were punished: ﴿بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾, that is, of transgressions, attributing it to the hands because most work is done with them, ﴿إذا هُمْ﴾, that is, after the calamity's existence has distressed them with distress, they forgot through it the blessings with which they had been entrusted and the adornments of generosity with which they had been clothed, ﴿يَقْنَطُونَ﴾, that is, they suddenly despair, renewing that despair at every moment of its occurrence, even though they call upon their Lord to remove it and seek His help to avert it, while they continually witness the opposite of that in both aspects, in themselves and in others. For this reason He denounced their failure to see (p-96), indicating by the conjunction waw that the sense is: "Did they not see in themselves the change of states?", saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 37:

﴿Have they not seen﴾, that is, by direct observation and by report, seeing repeatedly, [so that they come to know with a knowledge that, in its steadiness, is like the directly perceived thing. He expressed it with "seeing," which suits both the eye and insight (basirah), because the purpose of the surah is to establish that the whole matter belongs to God, and this requires nothing less than exerting effort and reflecting deeply. The context is a rebuke of despair (qunut), which is sufficient for the rest of direct observation because circumstances vary, unlike the surah of al-Zumar, whose purpose is to show the truth of the promise, for which mere knowledge suffices].

Since in the expansion and the contraction there is a combination of majesty (jalal) and beauty (jamal), he turned the speech by mentioning the all-comprehensive Name, and said: ﴿that God﴾, with His majesty and greatness, ﴿expands provision﴾, that is, increases it, ﴿for whomever He wills﴾, that is, among His servants, both among them and among others, ﴿and restricts it﴾, that is, narrows it. This is His constant way with one person at successive times, distant and near, and with different persons even at one time. So if they had considered His act of restriction, they would not have become insolent, and if they had considered His act of expansion, they would not have despaired. Rather, their condition would have been patience in trial, gratitude in ease, and abandoning the evil by which the decree had descended. Thus it is known from their condition that they are always bound to the present state.

They err concerning repeatedly observed matters, so there is no wonder in their being bound, in denying resurrection, to this present worldly life.

(p-97) Since their strength, the abundance of their intellect, the subtlety of their cunning [and the multitude] of their stratagems do not avail any one of them in securing provision, and their weakness, lack of intellect and incapacity of stratagem do not harm him, and since this was a great matter and a source, with its manifestness and majesty yet hidden and subtle, as one of them said:

Many an intelligent man whose ways have been baffled,
And a fool, a fool, you find him provided.

He, glorified is He, pointed to its greatness by His saying, emphasizing it, because their labor, in their intense concern for striving in this world, is the labor of one who thinks that attaining it depends only on the measure of effort in means: ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, that is, in this great matter, of restriction at one time and enrichment at another, of widening for one person and straitening for another, and of the security from the loss of present blessings despite repeated observation of loss in oneself and others, and the despair of their attainment at the time of trial despite frequent finding of relief, and other secrets of the verse, ﴿are signs﴾, that is, clear proofs of God's oneness, the completeness of His knowledge, the perfection of His power, and that there is truly no doer except Him. But they are for ﴿a people﴾, that is, people of resolve and sufficiency to undertake what is incumbent on them to undertake, ﴿who believe﴾, that is, who bring about this attribute and keep renewing it at every time, because of the proofs that continually present themselves to them, through continued contemplation and deep reflection, and reliance regarding provision on the One who said: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 17], that is, any seeker of knowledge who will be helped in it. So they do not rejoice in blessings when they come, fearing their loss if the Able wills it, nor grieve over them when they are gone, hoping for their return as a bounty from the Provider, because "the best of worship is waiting for relief." Rather, with what is upon them of the duties of worship, obligatory and recommended, they devote themselves to these and turn away from all else, having entrusted the matter of provision to the One who has taken charge of it, finished its apportioning, and undertaken its guarantee, and He is the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing.

Now when this has made clear the disregard for the world, since caring for it does not increase it and neglecting it does not diminish it, so that this yields nothing but hastening the distress of toil and fatigue, and since it was previously mentioned that sin is among the causes of loss of blessing, He consequently ordered the turning to spending it on its rightful dues, turning away from it, announcing its humiliation, and affirming with certainty that this is its true fulfilment, its investment, and its growth. So He said, addressing specifically the one most fit among the addressed to carry out His commands, because that falls more effectively upon the hearts of the followers and is more worthy of their good acceptance and hearing: ﴿So give﴾ O best of creation! ﴿to the near of kin his due﴾, beginning with him because he is the most deserving of people of righteousness [being] the joining of ties of kinship, and generosity and magnanimity, ﴿and the needy﴾ whether or not he is of the near of kin, ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, who is the traveller likewise. The due mentioned for these two, the apparent meaning is that it is meant as voluntary charity (nafl) and not obligatory (wajib), because the remaining categories are not mentioned; and the poor entered by way of priority.

When He commanded giving, He encouraged it, saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, the giving of high rank, ﴿is better﴾. And since He, glory be to Him, is the most self-sufficient of the self-sufficient, He accepts only what is purely for His sake, with no showing-off in it, He said, making known that this is not confined to those who were addressed specifically, but that everyone who follows their example will attain its blessing: ﴿for those who desire﴾, in the plural form. And since parting with wealth is extremely difficult, He encouraged it by mentioning the Face, which is the most noble aspect of a thing, here expressed as the essence, and by repeating the greatest name familiar to all creation, saying: ﴿the Face of Allah﴾, that is, the majesty of the Supreme King, so that they recognise of His right what dissolves before them over everything else, and thus they devote themselves sincerely to Him. ﴿And those﴾, the high-ranking, because of their independence from every perishable thing, ﴿they are﴾ exclusively ﴿the successful﴾ [that is], those whose success is not tainted by any loss. As for others, they are losers. As for one who does not spend, that is clear. As for one who spends in a manner of showing-off, by reputation and display, he has lost his wealth and left its burden upon himself. As for one who spends in the manner of true showing-off, he has explicitly stated it, making clear its great abomination, turning the address away from the noble station toward which he was turned, to make clear the exalted nature of His presence above it, and after that lofty resolve and pure, clean disposition, to the direction of those among whom such a thing is possible, and so He said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 39:

﴿Whatever you give﴾, i.e., whatever you bring [i.e., whatever you do], according to the reading of Ibn Kathir with the short vowel (qasr), so that it encompasses the giver, the taker, and the one who causes it to happen; or "you have given," according to the reading of others with the long vowel (madd). ﴿Of riba﴾, i.e., wealth given in the manner of prohibited (muharram) or disliked (makruh) riba, which is to give a gift in order to receive more in return for it. This was among the things forbidden to the Prophet ﷺ as an honour to him, and disliked for the general population. According to Ibn Kathir's reading with the short vowel, the meaning is: whatever you bring of giving with the intention of riba, ﴿that it may increase﴾, i.e., that what you have given or done may grow and multiply, or that you yourselves may increase it. This is according to the reading of the Medinans and Ya'qub with an upper-vowelled ta (fawqaniyya madmuma), from aroba (to increase). ﴿In the wealth of people﴾ [i.e., an increase occurs in it, with the wealth of people as its container; this is a metaphor for] the fact that the increase which the one who takes riba takes from their wealth is not truly owned by him at all. ﴿So it does not increase﴾, i.e., does not thrive and grow, ﴿with Allah﴾, i.e., the Supreme King who possesses absolute self-sufficiency and all attributes of perfection; and whatever does not increase with Allah is not blessed but rather destroyed, having no existence, for it is headed to annihilation however much it multiplies. ﴿Allah destroys riba and causes charities to increase﴾ [al-Baqarah: 276].

When he mentioned that whose increase is a loss, he followed it with that whose loss is an increase, and said: ﴿Whatever you give﴾, i.e., what you give for the sake of charity, as an agreed-upon norm, lest it give the impression of encouragement to take zakat, ﴿of zakat﴾, i.e., alms; he expressed it by this term to convey purity and increase, meaning you purify your wealth thereby from doubtful matters, your bodies from the substances of impurity, and your characters from rancour and defilement. Since sincerity is rare, he indicated its greatness by repeating it, and said: ﴿you seek﴾, i.e., by it, ﴿the face of Allah﴾, sincerely, keeping in mind His majesty, greatness and perfection; and he expressed the Essence by "face" because it is that which honours its possessor and which one feels shy before when seeing it, and it is the most noble part of the Essence.

Since the original would have been "then you," he turned away from it to a form that indicates His exaltation by shifting to addressing those present in His presence from among His close ones and angels, because the one who acts must have a tongue of truth (lisan sidq) among creatures through his deed, so how much more so when it comes from the Creator; and by pointing to Him with the distal demonstrative, to inform of the loftiness of His rank, and that the one addressed with giving is many while the doer is few and magnificent, he said: ﴿Then those﴾. Perhaps the singular address here is to encourage giving, in that none understands what is due to its people in its proper understanding except the one upon whom this revelation was sent down ﷺ. ﴿They are﴾, i.e., exclusively, ﴿the multipliers﴾, i.e., those who multiply their wealth in this world through that preservation and blessing, and in the Hereafter through abundant reward with Allah, from ten times up to what has no limit, as it is said: "muqawwin" (one with strength), "musir" (one with wealth), "musammin" (one with fattened camels), and "mu'attash" (one with thirst), for one who has strength, wealth, fatness in his camels, thirst, and the like.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 40:

When he had made clear by this that there is no increase except what Allah grants, and no good except what Allah chooses, and that this discourages excessive preoccupation with seeking worldly life, he explained this by a way clearer than which there is none, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., by the greatness of His majesty and none other, ﴿is the One who created you﴾, i.e., brought you into existence in the state of measured form you are in, while you possess nothing.

Since provision is distributed among people, and indeed is restricted for many of them despite its abundance, the provision of one who is newly born, especially if he is the son of a poor man, was considered unlikely. He pointed to it with the particle of distance, saying: ﴿Then He provided for you﴾. Since causing the death of one who is empowered in his body, mind, strength and the means of his nobility is wondrous, he drew attention to it by saying: ﴿Then He causes you to die﴾. Since all of that is in reality easy for Him, and since restoring life after death, if it is not easier than bringing about life the first time, is at least like it, even if they consider it unlikely, He said: ﴿Then He will bring you back to life﴾.

Since what he mentioned encompasses all their essences and states, and since a partner is one who takes part in some of the action or what is acted upon, and since it is known that their associates have no kind of making in any of that, he said, denouncing them: ﴿Is there any of﴾. Since their associating what they associate produced no fruit except that they assigned to them a portion of their wealth, he expressed it by saying: ﴿your associates﴾, i.e., those whom you claim to be partners, ﴿who does any of that﴾, indicating the loftiness of His rank by the particle of distance and by addressing everyone. Since the interrogation that denounces and rebukes carries the sense of negation, he stressed it, encompassing everything that is possible from it even if it is very little, saying: ﴿any of﴾, i.e., deserving this description you attribute to them.

Since they were necessarily obliged to say, "No, by Your might! Neither they nor any of them have any share in any of that by way of action," he pointed to the enormity of what they committed by what this proof produced. He said, turning away from them, increasing in exaltation and magnificence, exalting His noble self above them with a transcendence by the remoteness of His lofty rank from their state: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, i.e., He is exalted with a transcendence that description cannot encompass, above needing a partner, for that is a great deficiency. Since one who reports that He did something, or that He will do it, such as causing death and life, or resurrection and other things, is not prevented from it by an opposer, such as a partner or the like, He said: ﴿and exalted is He﴾, i.e., with an exaltedness to which minds cannot attain, as the form of the verbal pattern indicates. The reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i was with the second person in the past style, while the reading of the rest with the third person, with turning away out of anger, in His saying, expressing it in the present tense to indicate that it is not the nature of a rational person to commit shirk at all, how much more so when it is by way of renewal and continuity: ﴿above what they associate﴾, in that they would do anything of that or be able by any kind of power to prevent Him from anything He wills, so that they would thereby deserve to be magnified in any sort of magnification. So they declared Him exalted and magnified Him by disavowing every deity other than Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 41:

When He, glorified is He, had shown them the worthlessness of their associates, which should have led them to turn back, and they did not do so, He followed this with what afflicted them, unlike what had befallen their forefathers, as a punishment for their ugly deeds, seeking to incline them toward repentance. So He said: ﴿Corruption has appeared﴾, that is, deficiency in everything that benefits creation, ﴿on the land﴾ through drought, fear and the like, ﴿and the sea﴾ through drowning and the scarcity of benefits from fishing and the like, of everything that used to be obtained from them before. Al-Baghawi said: "The land (al-barr) refers to the open countryside and the deserts, and the sea (al-bahr) refers to the cities and the villages situated on flowing waters." Ikrimah said: "The Arabs call a metropolis a sea (bahr)."

Then He explained its cause by His saying: ﴿by what﴾. Since the context, by its indication of evil deeds, makes the verb's derivative form (al-iftি'āl) unnecessary, He said: ﴿have earned﴾, that is, have done (ʿamilat) (p-105) of evil a deed which, owing to their intense eagerness for it, even if it was of the lowest kinds, is indicated by the bare form of the verb (tajrīd al-fiʿl), as if it were poured from a height, and, owing to the intense perfection of its evil, as if it were cast in a mould.

Since most actions are done by the hand, He attributed to it what is meant as the whole, explicitly stating the generality of everything that has the capacity for motion, so He said: ﴿the hands of people﴾, that is, as a punishment for them for their deeds. Having mentioned its initial cause (al-ʿillah al-bidāʾiyyah), He followed it with the retributive cause (al-ʿillah al-jazāʾiyyah), so He said: ﴿that He may make them taste﴾ [Fussilat: 16], that is, by what We possess of greatness, in the recitation of Qunbul from Ibn Kathir with the nun (nūn), to show greatness in the tasting for some and pardon for others. The recitation of the rest is with the yāʾ (ya'), according to the pattern of the past majesty (al-jalālah). He indicated His generosity, glorified is He, by His saying: ﴿some of what they did﴾, that is, its consequence, its heat and its burning, and He pardons much, either entirely and completely, or by hastening it and delaying it to some time in this world or to the Hereafter. What is meant is the recompense with the like of their actions, a recompense for them, expressing the caused by the cause that they inflicted upon people, so that when they seize property they may know the measure of what those whom they seized from have tasted, and when a close relative of theirs is killed, they may feel the heat of what the close relative of those they killed suffered, and similar to that of what they made light of when they inflicted severe harm on others while they were laughing and wondering (p-106) at his distress and mocking, heedless of the intensity of what he suffers of kinds of burning, he and whoever is dear to him, whose affair concerns him and whose matter is important to him, while his hand has been shackled from helping by helplessness and his reach shortened by weakness and subjugation. Then He added a third cause, the final cause (al-ʿillah al-ghāʾiyyah), so He said: ﴿so that they may return﴾, that is, so that their condition in the eyes of whoever looks at them becomes the condition of one whose return is hoped for from doing the like of that, out of fear that the like of that recompense be repeated upon them.

Because humans, in their deficiency and their attachment to particulars, cling strongly to empirical reasoning, and because their knowledge of the days of past peoples and the events of earlier generations was sufficient to admonish them into turning back from their beliefs and renouncing their obstinacy, yet when they did not look at the traces of those peoples with consideration and reflection and remembrance, they were counted among those who had not seen them, God, glory be to Him, drew attention to this by veiling Himself from them with the veil of might. He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to order them to travel to observe, so He said, emphasizing the meaning of the preceding speech, as counsel to them and gentleness toward them: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these people whose only concern is the world, who do not pass from the outward to the inward in what they look at: ﴿Travel﴾. And He indicated that the dwellings of those destroyed span every boundary around them in all directions, as has already passed, so He said: ﴿in the earth﴾, for your past journeying, since it was not accompanied by a lesson, amounts to nothing.

Since the intended aim is submission to monotheism, and He had reminded them of what befell them in the manner of what befell the earlier peoples, He said: ﴿Then look﴾, with the fa' of sequence. And since what He brought down upon them was of extreme severity, He made them know it by this, and He framed it in the form of a question, to frighten them lest they be struck with its like, so He said: ﴿how﴾. And since their punishment was awesome and their matter severe and grievous, He indicated it by making the verb masculine, so He said: ﴿was the end of﴾, that is, the final outcome of ﴿those﴾. And since the intended ones were groups of the punished, and they were some of those who had passed, not all of time, He made it partial and said: ﴿before﴾, that is, before your days, God made them taste the evil consequence of their affair, and cast them into the pits of their scheming.

Since this admonition was sufficient for consideration, the hearer would be expected to say: "I have reflected and seen their traces to be great, and their craftsmanship firm, yet their cities are empty and their houses desolate, they were struck with the whip of punishment, so ruin and destruction engulfed them. Why, then, were they punished?" So He answered with His saying: ﴿Most of them were polytheists﴾. Therefore We destroyed them, and their multitude did not avail them, and We saved the believers, and their fewness did not harm them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 43:

When they, despite their frequent passing by their dwellings, their looking upon their traces, and their hearing of their news, did not take heed, it was indicated that they were nonexistent, by turning the address away from them and directing it to the obedient listener. So He said, making it a consequence of what preceded of establishing the proofs (p-108) and of admonition and warning: ﴿So set your face﴾, that is, O you who alone understands Us in the true understanding, because We have preferred you over all creation, ﴿toward the religion, upright﴾, which has no crookedness in any respect, but is entirely justice, from disavowal of idols to adorning oneself with the station of excellence (ihsan). So hold fast to it, make it before your eyes, do not neglect it even for the blink of an eye, because it is easy in what its causes help with, outwardly through the clear exposition in which there is no obscurity, and inwardly through being innately disposed to it, so that even the blind, the deaf, and the mute accept it, and it becomes in it like a mountain in firmness.

Since keeping to uprightness is rare, He repeated the warning to preserve its people. So He said, making the matter easy by not encompassing time, by affixing the preposition, indicating contentment with a little of action, even if it were an hour of a day, on the condition that it continues until death: ﴿before﴾, and He unfolded the verbal noun for clarity, so He said: ﴿that there comes a day﴾, that is, a great day, which is the Day of Resurrection, or death, and He indicated His sole sovereignty with His saying: ﴿no repelling of it﴾. The speech shifts, in the reading of Qunbul, from the manifestation of greatness to what is greater than it, as the situation requires; and it is made explicit in the reading of the rest, lest one suppose the pronoun refers back to the religion, so He said: ﴿from Allah﴾. And if He Himself does not repel it, since He promised to bring it, and He is Possessor of Majesty (p-109) and Honour, then who could repel it?

When He affirmed its coming, He detailed its matter, encouraging and warning, so He said: ﴿On that day﴾, that is, when it comes, ﴿they will be divided﴾, that is, all creatures will separate into a division that may be hidden from some of them, as indicated by the idghām, and they will say: "What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?"

Since the meaning is that they are a group in the Garden and a group in the Blaze, al-Biqa'i explains this by stating the outcome of its cause, in answer to someone who seems to ask: "Where do they separate?" He says: ﴿Whoever disbelieves﴾, that is, among them [who does something], ﴿his disbelief is upon him﴾, that is, not upon anyone else [his disbelief is his own burden]. Against their own souls they transgress, and for them they lay low (the ground), so they will arrive on that Day at the Fire which they used to deny. Whoever has his disbelief upon him, which has destroyed him, until death, has no deliverance after the passing (of life). He used a singular pronoun, referring it back to the wording "whoever" (man), to state explicitly that each person is repaid for his own deed, not the group as a group. It also conveys that the disbelievers are few, even if they are more numerous than the believers, because they have no protector, and because their word is divided: ﴿You think them united, but their hearts are scattered﴾ [al-Hashr: 14] [the verse and]. And because there is no gathering among the people of the Fire, so that some of them console themselves with others; rather, each of them is occupied with his own concern, preventing him from knowing what happens to others. ﴿And whoever does righteousness﴾, that is, with faith and what follows from it. He stated it explicitly and did not use a pronoun, lest it be supposed that the pronoun returns to ﴿whoever disbelieves﴾, and as good news that the people of the Garden are many, even if they are few, because Allah is their protector, so He purifies them and supports them. In combining the reward (in the plural) with the singular conditional, there is an encouragement to act without looking to a helper, since it benefits himself and others, because the believer to the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another. The least benefit is that it benefits his parents and his teacher through that deed. He expressed it with "souls" (nafs) so that it would indicate, after indicating the will of the doer and those who support him, to the point that by the unity of intention they are as one, that righteous deeds purify the souls and cleanse them from base morals. So He said: ﴿Then for their own souls﴾, that is, specifically their deeds [and for them specifically is the fruit of their righteous deed], and for their own souls ﴿they lay down a bed﴾, that is, they prepare and make ready abodes in the graves and in the Garden, and even in this world, for Allah honours them with the honour of His obedience. The verse is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one element is omitted where its counterpart is present, and vice versa): He first omitted their transgression against their own souls because of what is indicated by "laying down a bed," and secondly omitted that the deed is specific to them because of what is indicated by the fact that disbelief falls upon its bearer alone. [And better than this is to say: He mentioned disbelief, which is the cause, as an indication of faith in the second place, and righteous deeds, which are the fruit, in the second place as an indication of the evil deed in the first place.]

When he had finished explaining their splitting apart, he mentioned its cause, saying: ﴿That He may reward﴾, that is, God, glorified is He, who sent down this surah to show that He gives victory to His allies because of their good deeds, for He is with the good-doers. For this reason He limited the mention here to them, saying: ﴿those who believe﴾, that is, even at the lowest level, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, that is, in confirmation of their faith, ﴿righteous deeds.﴾ Since the deeds themselves are a blessing from Him, so that the reward is pure grace, He said: ﴿from His bounty.﴾

Since their being granted delight is among the greatest punishments for the disbelievers, who used to mock them and laugh at them, he gave the reason with an emphatic statement, against the claim of one who thinks that the world's turning toward the disobedient is due to God's love for them: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.﴾ That is, He does not treat those who are deeply rooted in disbelief as one who loves them does, so He does not place them on a level with the believers. From this is understood what He withheld of their recompense, so the verse belongs to the category of al-ihtibak (a device in which two statements are given, each omitting something, and their arrangement is such that what is affirmed in each indicates what is omitted from the other). The implied sense here is: after mentioning the reward of those who believed, that He loves the believers and, by His justice, requites those who disbelieved and did evil deeds (p-112), because He does not love the disbelievers. He changed the arrangement so that, while it indicates this, as you see, it also points to what was omitted, and to the fact that honouring the believers is the primary aim, which is itself the humbling of the disbelievers. He expressed the side of the believers by the ultimate end, which is the intended meaning of God's love, because it is more pleasing; and on the side of the disbelievers by the starting point, which is a metaphor, because it is more stinging and harmful.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 46:

When He concluded, at the beginning of the surah, the signs indicating divine unity, which entail the Resurrection (because the Resurrection brings the complete manifestation of wisdom and the lifting of the veil from hearts regarding the attributes of majesty, namely that the heavens and the earth stand by His command), He followed this with what is most closely bound to it. He concluded it with some of the disbelievers after mentioning the Day of Resurrection, and then He followed it with mention of that by which the existence of creation is sustained, namely the winds. He makes them a means of bringing down blessings, among which is what is greatest as evidence for the Resurrection, namely vegetation. All of these together are evidence of that, and a cause of settling on land and of sailing at sea, which conveys the benefits of some lands to others. By this, affairs are ordered for the people of the earth. The believer among them uses the reason that Allah, glorified is He, has granted him to reflect on this, until it leads him to thank Him, so He loves him. The disbeliever restricts himself to the habitual toil in seeking those blessings and multiplying them, so this makes him arrogant, which leads him to disbelief, so He hates him. The winds also resemble people most closely: some of them are greatly beneficial, and some of them cause great harm. [So] He said: ﴿And among His signs﴾, i.e., the clear indications that point to the perfection of His power and the completeness of His knowledge, which indicate that He alone is the One who established this existence. Just as He established it, so He establishes another existence, which is the essence of the matter and the focal point of wisdom, and more wondrous than this existence, in which creatures are raised after their annihilation, and He manifests Himself to decide judgment among them, so He takes justice for their oppressed from their oppressors. Then He separates them, so that a group [of them] is in Paradise, the abode of help and honor, and a group in the Blaze, the cave of humiliation and reproach. ﴿that He sends the winds﴾ in a manner of renewal and continuity, and they are all except the south wind (ad-dabbur), which is referred to in the noble hadith as something to seek refuge from:

"O Allah, make them winds of mercy and do not make them winds of punishment."

My explanation of it at ﴿And He it is who sends the winds as good tidings﴾ [an-Naml: 63] in Surah an-Naml has already been sufficient. In using the plural here, on which there is consensus, because it is described with the plural, there is an indication of the striking power, for turning a single wind from one direction to another is a great matter, and no one other than Him has power over it in the vast expanse of the sky. Likewise stilling it. How much more so when the winds are opposing, so in stirring them in this way and then stilling them there is [something] of striking power that none knows except people of insight. ﴿as bearers of good news﴾, i.e., for you, of everything in which lies your benefit, of rain, of spirit, of coolness of hearts and of the pleasure of life.

Since the implied meaning is: "that He may destroy by them whom He wills of His servants," or "that He may ward off from you what would result from their absence of His vengeance, namely heat, and what follows from it of the spread of corrupting things and the decay of beneficial things," and He omitted this because the context is about mentioning blessings, He followed it with His saying, affirming the lām for clarification of what was joined to: ﴿and that He may make you taste﴾ of His mercy. He indicated the greatness of His blessings by the partitive in His saying ﴿of His mercy﴾ [i.e., His blessings], namely sweet waters, moist trees, soundness of bodies, fertility of times, and what follows from these matters that none can count except their Creator, and none can conceive of them as they truly should be conceived except one who has lost the winds: from the existence of spirit, the purity of the land, the removal of corruption [from the air], assistance in winnowing grains, and other things. He indicated the greatness of this blessing, and that it has become, because of the abundance of familiarity, something overlooked, by repeating the lām, so He said: ﴿and that the ships may run﴾, i.e., the ships in all seas and whatever is like them when they blow.

Since He attributed the running to the ships, He removed it from them by His saying ﴿by His command﴾, i.e., by what is suitable of gentle winds; and if He wills, He makes them violent so that they are drowned, or He makes them opposing so that they are bewildered and tossed back and forth, until the sailors resort to every stratagem to halt the ships so that they are not destroyed.

Since each of the mere sailing at sea and the reaching by it from one city [to another city] is a blessing in itself, He joined to "that they may run" His saying, drawing attention by repeating the lām for clarification of what was joined to [for the magnification of the blessing]: ﴿and that you may seek﴾, i.e., seek with diligent seeking by that voyage, and the greatness of what is with Him, by the partitive in His saying ﴿of His bounty﴾, from what He subjects for you of the wind for travel to markets from city to city, and for jihad and other things. ﴿And that perhaps you may be thankful﴾, i.e., and that you would be, when He does this for you, in hope [that] you will ﴿give thanks﴾ for what He has poured upon you of His blessings, [and warded off from you of His punishments].

(p-116) When the implied sense is: "So He lets whoever He wills taste of His mercy, and sends down His vengeance upon whoever disbelieves," and the whole context concerns the victory of His allies and the subjugation of His enemies, and the winds are "bearers of good tidings and bearers of warning" like the messengers, and they are described as good, as in the Sahih from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her): "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when Jibril (peace be upon him) met him, was more generous with good than the wind sent forth," and [the winds] in the abundance and generality of their benefits, if they are beneficial, and their harms, if they are harmful, are most like the messengers in giving life to one people and destroying others, and in what arises from them, as (p-116) what arises from the messengers.

As the Prophet (ﷺ) said, in what al-Shaykhān narrated from Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him): al-Bukhārī in "al-ʿIlm" and Muslim in "al-Manāqib": "The likeness of what Allah has sent me with of guidance and knowledge is like abundant rain that fell upon a land. A part of it was good, so it accepted the water and produced grass and abundant vegetation. Another part of it was hard ground (ajādib) that held the water, so Allah benefited people with it: they drank, gave drink, and planted. And it fell upon another part, which was barren plains (qīʿān) that hold no water and produce no grass. That is the likeness of one who comprehends the religion of Allah and benefits from what Allah has sent me with, so he knows and teaches; and the likeness of one who does not raise his head to that and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I was sent."

When the matter is so, it is coordinated (ʿaṭafa) with His words ﴿He helps whom He wills﴾ [al-Rūm: 5] and His words ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾ [al-Rūm: 10], or with what its implied sense causes, as a consequence of His words ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾ [al-Rūm: 43]: ﴿And We have certainly sent you as a bringer of good tidings to whoever obeys with good, and a warner to whoever disobeys with evil.﴾ This is His word, consoling this noble Prophet, upon whom be the best of prayers and peace, and his followers. He turned the speech to the station of majesty (ʿaẓamah), since the context of vengeance requires it, and He emphasized it to indicate that the situation, with its intensification, reached the state of despair; or to deny the great number of people who denied that messengers could be human. ﴿And We have certainly sent﴾ with the might that belongs to Us.

Since the concern is to inform that His custom has continued, from ancient times to the present, in giving victory to His allies, He said, instructing by placing the prepositional phrase first, that sending in fact did not extend over the span of the past: ﴿from before you﴾, placed before ﴿messengers﴾; or that the speech concerns specifically the destroyed nations. Or [it is] to alert that he is the Seal of the Prophets, by restricting the sending of others to the time before his. He said ﴿to their peoples﴾ to inform that when the might of Allah comes, neither the near nor the far can benefit from it. And in the consolation he added the reminder, indicating the severity of the people's harm to their prophets, since He did not say "to her people."

Since the sending of Allah is necessarily a cause for the clarity that leaves no confusion, He said: ﴿Then they brought them the clear proofs﴾, so their people divided into believers and criminals. ﴿Then We took vengeance﴾, i.e., the hostility of the believers toward the criminals regarding Us became a cause, because We took vengeance with the greatness that is Ours ﴿upon those who committed crimes﴾ because of their crime, which is severing what We commanded them to join, the necessary result of which is joining what they were commanded to sever: they joined disbelief and severed faith. So We forsook them. And it was a truth upon Us to subdue the criminals, as an honor to those who opposed them for Our sake, and We bestowed favor upon those who believed, so We gave them victory.

Since the focal point of the benefit is His (glorified be He) binding Himself to what He has graciously bestowed, He put it first (p-118) to hasten joy and to comfort souls, so He said: ﴿And it was⦆ i.e., by way of permanence and continuity ﴿a truth upon Us⦆ i.e., by what We made obligatory through Our promise, which admits no breach ﴿to help the believers⦆ i.e., both groups in that description, in this world and in the Hereafter. This has never ceased to be Our practice with every religious community throughout the ages, for this is from the wisdom that should not be neglected. So let these people prepare for the like of this, and let them take its readiness, so they may see who is the defeated, and whether anything will benefit them.

The verse is of the figure called iḥtibāk (interweaving): the destruction, which is the effect of forsaking, was omitted first, because the mention of victory indicates it; and second, the bestowal of blessing was omitted, because the mention of vengeance indicates it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 48:

When He, glory be to Him, had established the proof for the Resurrection and for the existence of creation through His directing of the winds as He wills, and had followed it with the verse of consolation and warning, and the punishment of those mentioned in it was by the wind, or was caused by it, or had some connection with it, He followed that with the announcement that He alone, glory be to Him, is the one who has this power. This was to draw attention to the greatness of the sign of the winds, and to urge reflection upon it, confirming and explicitly stating the matter of the Resurrection. So He said, a second time, speaking of the station of majesty that the punishment required, to the Greatest Name, the all-comprehensive one, whose regard is more toward blessing than toward retribution: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿who sends﴾ time after time, because He is the one uniquely perfect, so there is none equal to Him, ﴿the winds﴾, agitated and stirred up after having been still. In the reading of the majority (al-Jumhur) it is in the plural, unlike Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, as an indication of the greatness of the workmanship, in that He does what He has mentioned with whatever wind He wishes. ﴿So they raise up clouds﴾ which had no existence before.

When He attributed the raising to the winds, He withdrew the attribution to them in the spreading and the breaking up, for He did not place in them any power over any of that, so that it would be known that the whole of it is His act. So He said: ﴿then He spreads it﴾ after its gathering ﴿in the sky﴾, that is, in the direction of the height.

Since the matter of the cloud is extremely wondrous in its existence after not having been, and its forms, its colours, and all its conditions, in its gathering and its dispersal, [and its density], and what is in it of rain, thunder, lightning and other things which none knows in their true knowledge except Allah, the Exalted, He indicated all of that by the interrogative particle, although they have counted it [here] as a conditional particle. So He said: ﴿how﴾, that is, as ﴿He wills﴾, in whatever direction He wills [a little at a time], sometimes as far as an hour's or a day's journey, and at other times much further, as far as days' journey, in differing states, which shows you with certainty that He alone did it by His choice, with no part in it for nature or anything else.

Since what was meant by that is that it is in the state of continuity, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿and He makes it﴾, that is, when He wills, ﴿fragments﴾, that is, pieces not joined to one another (p. 120) in a joining that prevents the descent of water, ﴿then you see﴾, that is, by means of Allah's sending it, or by means of His making it full of pores and openings, O you who possess the capacity of sight, or O noblest of our creation, whom none other knows in its true knowledge, ﴿the rain﴾, that is, the falling drops, near and abundant, ﴿coming out from within it﴾, that is, from within the cloud, which is a collective noun, in both states of being joined and separated.

Since He, glory be to Him, had caused by that the joy of His servants at what they hope for from its effect, although they often witness the failure of the effect because of obstacles which He brings about, He said, causing it to follow from that, indicating with the particle of certainty His great favour and the certainty of His bounty: ﴿then when He strikes with it﴾ [that is, Allah] ﴿whomever﴾ of the lands ﴿He wills﴾, and He drew attention to the fact that this is a favour from Him, which is not obligatory upon Him toward anyone at all, by His saying: ﴿of His servants﴾, that is, those whose worship has never ceased to be obligatory upon them, and who are deserving of constant gratitude to Him and submission to His command, specifically for them by His power and choice. He made clear their levity by their haste to rejoicing despite the possibility of blights, comprehending in that a response to the meaning of "whomever" or to "the servants," since levity from a group is more shameful. So He said: ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾, that is, the glad tidings appear upon them, which is the joy by which the skin brightens at the time of the striking, appearing in a very great and evident manner, [because of] what they hope for from what arises from it of beneficial effect, of fertility, moisture and softness;

Then He explained their levity and helplessness by His saying: ﴿And indeed﴾, that is, while the state of affairs was that they ﴿had been﴾ in the past time with a condition firmly established within their souls, and the nearness of their despair to their joy indicates the swiftness of their emotional reaction and the great frequency of their fluctuation, with the preposition [min], so He said: ﴿before it was sent down﴾, that is, the rain, in the easiest manner in which He, glory be to Him, could send it, ﴿upon them﴾. Then He confirmed the great extent of their fickleness and their lack of power by His saying: ﴿before it﴾, that is, before the joy, other than it, without any interval of time in which it could be claimed that they had any causal role in the rain, ﴿were indeed despairing﴾, that is, silent about what was in their souls, bewildered, hopeless and cut off, so they had no way to bring about anything of that sort, nor did their objects of worship have any capacity for it, either independently or as a means.

When this veil was lifted and doubts were removed, He, glorified is He, turned away from them, on the premise that "tara" (you see) is addressed to one who has the capacity for sight, indicating that they have no understanding. He turned to the essence of the good creation fit to receive [from Him], saying, as a consequence of that: ﴿So look﴾. Since the purpose is to magnify the blessing, and provision is greater than creation, He used the particle of limit [to indicate] contemplating the furthest after contemplating the nearest, so He said: ﴿at the traces﴾. Since there was no cause for this other than His mercy preceding His wrath, He said: ﴿of the mercy of Allah﴾, comprising the essentials of admonition. He stated it explicitly and did not use a pronoun, to draw attention (p-122) to what in that is of supreme greatness: the diversity of crops after the watering of the earth, its stirring with vegetation, the greening of trees, the variety of fruits, and the emergence of all of them from that water.

Since this is among the great extraordinary things, but it has been repeated until it became familiar, He drew attention to its greatness by indicating that it is worthy of being asked about, so He said: ﴿how He gives life﴾, i.e., this trace or Allah, time after time, ﴿to the earth﴾ by bringing forth what has been mentioned from it.

Since His power to renew its revival is constant, as the present tense indicates and the aim of the surah calls for, He indicated that also by omitting the preposition, so He said: ﴿after its death﴾ by its annihilation of that.

Since this indicates the power to restore the dead, and it is necessarily like it, for everything that humans do not cause to grow scatters over the earth after becoming dry stubble that the winds scatter, and crumbles until it becomes dust. When water descends upon it, it returns as it was or better. He said: ﴿Indeed, that﴾, i.e., the One of great affair who is capable of this, ﴿is surely the Giver of life to the dead﴾, all of them, of animals and plants; i.e., He is still capable of that, and this attribute is established for Him and continues. ﴿And He﴾ (p-123) ﴿over everything﴾ of that and other things ﴿is All-Powerful﴾, because the relation of power from Him, glorified is He, to every possible thing is equal.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 51:

Since seeing the repeated manifestations of such power does not give them knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, He indicated this by His saying, turning the speech toward the context of majesty to alert to the greatness of His pardon, may He be glorified, together with the completeness of His power. He emphasized it to the utmost degree of emphasis, to alert that it is not the way of people of intellect to fail to benefit from admonitions. He expressed it with the particle of doubt, to alert that His bounty is greater than His retribution. He confirmed it with an oath, given their denial of disbelief: ﴿And if We send﴾ after the existence of this good effect, ﴿a wind﴾ barren, ﴿and they see it﴾, meaning the effect. It is also permissible that the pronoun refers to the wind, through the expression of the cause for the effect, ﴿yellowed﴾, meaning it has withered and begun to perish from the severity of the wind's dryness, whether by heat or by cold, ﴿they would surely continue﴾, meaning they would persist, and by Our might over it, they would renew their disbelief forever. Although "ẓalla" means to remain during the day, he expressed it with the past tense in place of the future, as in the phrase "li-yaẓallanna wallāhi" (by Allah, he will surely remain), for emphasis on its certainty. Perhaps he expressed it with "ẓulūl" (remaining), because the period of sleep has no renewal of disbelief in it. For this reason he used the partitive particle (ḥarf al-tab'īḍ, the particle indicating a part) when he said: ﴿after it﴾, meaning after its yellowing, ﴿they disbelieve﴾, through their despair of Allah's mercy and their denial of the blessings He had previously bestowed upon them, after His repeated making Himself known to them, may He be glorified, with kindness, [p. 124] after the two rings of the saddle-girth had joined (i.e., after the hardship had come to an end). And [it was, and it was]. So they neither gave thanks for the mercy in times of ease, nor were patient in the calamity of adversity. Rather, they did not increase there beyond rejoicing, nor did they diminish here anything of renewing disbelief and persisting in it. So they did not cease, because of their lack of insight, to remain in the blameworthy condition, and they did not hasten to remove the afflictions, [nor to obtain the blessings, so they were more astray than the cattle].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 52:

When all of this about their condition, namely their quick shifting between grief and joy in times of hardship and ease, and their persistence in renewing disbelief, was evidence of the lightness of their intellects and the poor quality of their reflection, since they neither heed the visible signs nor listen to the signs recited to them, He drew from this the explanation that their affair belongs to no one but Him, glorified is He, and that He has made them [dead] in meaning. He said, giving them the likeness of three kinds of people, and emphasizing it because they deny that their condition is like this while the Prophet (ﷺ) was exceedingly eager to make them hear and strove hard at it: ﴿Indeed you﴾, meaning, their persistence in this disbelief, sometimes in ease and sometimes in hardship, standing with the effect without looking at the one who produces it, while you recite to them His signs and alert them to the wonders of His clear proofs, by reason of the fact that you ﴿do not make the dead hear﴾, meaning it is not within your power to make hear those who have no life, so they have no sight and no hearing; or [the dead of] the hearts, [making them hear] in a way that benefits them, because this is among the things that He, glorified is He, has reserved for Himself. Some of these are like the dead, because God, exalted is He, has sealed their faculties. ﴿Nor make the deaf hear﴾, meaning you, in the recitation of the majority (qira'a, the standard transmitted reading) other than Ibn Kathir, ﴿the deaf﴾, meaning those who have no hearing at all. Ibn Kathir read the verb as from sami'a (to hear) and made ﴿the deaf﴾ the subject, so the sense becomes: indeed whoever has died, or whose heart has died, does not hear, and the deaf do not hear ﴿the call﴾ when you call them. Then, since the deaf person may perceive your call when he is facing you by his sense of sight, He said: ﴿when they turn away﴾. He used the verb and did not say (the feminine form) "wallat," to indicate the strength of the turning away, lest it be thought that it was applied to mere avoidance, for example. For this reason He formed from its doer a circumstantial state (hal, a grammatical term for a state-describing accusative), which is His saying: ﴿retreating﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 53:

When he began with the one who lacks the sense of hearing, because it is more beneficial (since man is distinguished from other animals only by speech), he followed it with the sense of sight, indicating by the placement of the pronoun that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) strives for their guidance with the striving of one who seems to be doing it himself, training others in moderation in affairs. So He said: ﴿And you cannot guide the blind﴾, meaning, you cannot bring about guidance for them, even if they hear. (p-126) This is the reading of the majority other than Hamzah. Hamzah read it as a present-tense verb addressed to the second person from hada (to guide), so the sense is: "And you do not renew the guidance of the blind ﴿from their error﴾ when they stray from the path and go far astray, even if it is a slight straying." This is indicated by the feminine form, and even if you exhaust yourself in advising them, they will not follow the path unless their hands are in your hand, and whenever you neglect them, and you are not a Guardian, they return to their error. So the negation in this sentence, in the reading of the majority, implies what the nominal sentence requires of continuity of guidance, emphasized; and Hamzah's reading implies what the present verb requires of renewal. In the previous one, the verbal present sentence implies renewal, as long as it is conditioned on turning away; and in the first, the renewal of hearing is absolute, so it is more eloquent. Then the one after it: the first category, [those who] do not accept good in any way, like Abu Jahl and Ubayy ibn Khalaf; the second, [those who] may approach in some way, like Utbah ibn Rabi'ah when he used to say to them: "Leave this man between himself and the people; if they overcome him, then he is what you want, and if not, his honor is your honor." The third are the hypocrites. He expressed all of them in the plural, because it is more stinging. And Allah is the Granter of success.

When that was a metaphor for their persistence in disbelief, he clarified it [by stating that the intended meaning is the death of the heart, its deafness and its blindness, not the literal sense] with His saying: ﴿If not﴾, meaning, you do not (p-127) ﴿make hear except those who believe﴾, meaning, who renew their faith continually, affirming ﴿Our signs﴾, meaning, in whom there is the capacity for that always; so he submits to the signs that are heard and takes heed from the signs that are made. He indicated with the singular in the condition that turning one individual from his opinion is closer than turning him when he is with others; and he indicated with the plural in the consequent that if this method is followed, the followers increase. So He said: ﴿So they﴾, meaning, as a result of their acceptance of that, they are ﴿submitting﴾, meaning, yielding to the proof with the utmost yielding, not rigid with blind imitation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 54:

When Allah (glorified is He) had demonstrated His power over resurrection through various kinds of evidence, sometimes in bodies and sometimes in faculties, and had multiplied in this surah the clear proofs for this, and concluded, because no one perceives these demonstrations except one whose disposition is sound, so that his temperament becomes pliant to the evidences, and his thought and reflection fly through the deserts of decrees on the wings of knowledge, He joined to that a comprehensive proof encompassing power over both substances and meanings, in both origination and return. For this reason He turned the speech to the all-comprehensive Name, and turned it to direct address for generality and for winning the heart through honour. So He said, emphasizing, as an indication that this is evidence of His power over resurrection, and that no one doubts it, though they deny it in effect, since neither of the two can be separated from the other: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who combines the attributes of perfection (p-128) [alone].

Since the definiteness of the relative pronoun is evident and unambiguous, he expressed it with it rather than with the active participle, and said: ﴿who created you﴾, that is, from non-existence. Since the seat of a human being's condition and the foundation and natural constitution upon which he rests is weakness, and his weakest state is at its beginning, He said: ﴿from weakness﴾, that is, weakness in general, in line with what the reading of Hamzah and ʿĀṣim (with variance from Ḥafṣ) with a fatḥah on the ḍād indicates; and strength is indicated by the reading of the rest with a ḍammah. Or [it means] from a despised water, through the stages that Allah willed, and then the age of the child that Allah willed.

Since strengthening the weak [meaning] is like reviving a dead body, He said: ﴿Then He made﴾, by means of a cause and a making, through development across the stages of creation by what He establishes of causes. Since the intended meaning is not totality, He expressed it with the preposition, and said: ﴿after﴾. Since the weakness from which strength arises is other than the first, He stated it explicitly and did not pronounce it as a pronoun, and said: ﴿weakness, strength﴾, with the magnitude of the body and the effect of the state of growing up, to strength by reaching completion at twenty-one years, which is the beginning of the age of youth, until the age of maturity by reaching full strength at [forty-two] years. Were it not for the repeated observation of this, the originating of it after its non-existence would be a breach of custom, like restoring an old man to youth after his decrepitude. ﴿Then He made after strength﴾ in youth, by which hearts are strengthened, noses are protected, and souls become proud because of it, ﴿weakness﴾, returning what He had brought you to, to the origin of your state.

Since whiteness of the hair generally results from weakness of temperament, He said: ﴿and gray hair﴾, which is whiteness in the hair arising from coldness and dryness of temperament, by which the body withers, and resolve and knowledge diminish. This occurs at the standing at forty-three, which is the first age of middle age, and by actual decline beginning after fifty, until the decline increases at sixty-three, which is the first age of old age, and weakness intensifies to what Allah the Exalted wills.

Since this is the prevailing custom, and people differ in it, and among people there is one who grows old while still strong, all of that produces, necessarily, the exercise of choice together with comprehensive knowledge and perfect power. So He said: ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, that is, of this and other than this, ﴿and He is the All-Knowing﴾, that is, the one who has reached complete knowledge, so He causes by the causes He wills, for what He wills to bring into being or to annihilate, ﴿the All-Powerful﴾, so no one can nullify any of His causes; therefore nothing He wills fails to occur at the time He wills it, at all. He placed the attribute of knowledge first because it entails power, which is the station's concern; so mentioning it is then an explicit statement after an allusion, and an expression after a hint.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 55:

(p-130) When His power over the resurrection and other matters was established, He linked it to His words at the beginning of the surah, ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be dumbfounded﴾ [al-Rum: 12], or to what is implied by: "So on the day He wills your death, you will die, not delaying from the moment of the term nor advancing it." His words ﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, i.e., the Resurrection (al-qiyamah), which is the re-creation of the creatures who had been (over thousands of years, gradually) and whose measure none knows except Allah, Exalted is He, in less than the blink of an eye. For this reason it is called "the Hour" (al-sa'ah), to inform of its ease for Him, glorified is He. ﴿The criminals will swear﴾, i.e., those who are deeply immersed in crime, following the habit of ignorance in asserting with certainty what they have no knowledge of: ﴿that﴾ they ﴿tarried﴾ in the world and the barzakh ﴿for no more than an hour﴾, i.e., a small portion of a night or a day.

Since this is a strange matter, being a false statement that brings about the greatest disgrace and humiliation before that great assembly, while it benefits them nothing, He resumed with His words, drawing attention to the fact that He is the one who causes it: so there is no wonder. ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., in the same way as that turning away from the realities of matters toward their doubts, ﴿they used to be﴾ in the world, in a state that became like their nature, ﴿turned away﴾, i.e., turned away from the truth, whose source is seeking honesty and submitting to the truth, toward falsehood, whose source is seeking mere contention, by Our turning them away (p-131), for there is no difference in Our power and Our knowledge between one life and another, or one abode and another. Perhaps He framed the verb in the passive to indicate how easily they submit to falsehood with whatever turner there may be.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 56:

When He had described the ignorant, He followed it with the description of the scholars, so He said: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say﴾. By His saying ﴿those who were given knowledge﴾ He drew attention to thanking the One who bestowed it upon them, and He cast the verb in the passive form to indicate that it is easy for them to acquire it, from the eminent and the lowly alike. He followed it with what is not illuminated by its lights and does not bring forth its fruits without it, so He said: ﴿and faith﴾, indicating their reflection upon all the clear and obscure signs, swearing [to the truth of their statement] just as those [others] had sworn, confirming their speech, facing the criminals in rebuke and reproach, affirming what those [others] had denied: ﴿You have indeed remained within the Book of God﴾, that is, within the decree of Him who possesses all perfection, which He recorded in His Book, the Book that informs the world, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And behind them is a barrier until the day they are resurrected﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 100]. As for determining the precise duration of the remaining, He concealed it from His servants. When the Qur'an had informed them that the ultimate end of the barrier is the Resurrection, and He had told the truth in His report, they made their statement a consequence of that, saying: ﴿So this﴾, that is, so there has occurred what we used to say and what you used to deny us concerning it, we tell you now, when you are no longer able to deny: this is ﴿the Day of Resurrection﴾, [that is] what we believed in and what you [used to] deny, and it has come exactly as we used to tell you. Thus the falsity of your claim has become clear, and you used to claim deliverance from it through various kinds of falsehoods, seeking to prevail; so what you would have done upon its presence, do it now. This is a warning to them that there is no benefit in pinpointing the length of the stay in the world or in the barrier; the benefit lies only in believing what the Book has reported, since belief is then beneficial. And since the implied meaning was: it has come just as we knew it would, so if you had any kind of knowledge you would have confirmed our report about it, and that would have benefited you now, He joined to it His saying: ﴿but you used to not know﴾, that is, a state that is like a natural disposition for you in your denial of it, ﴿you had no knowledge at all﴾, because of your neglect in seeking knowledge from its gates and reaching it through its causes. Therefore you denied it, and so you deserved the recompense of that Day.

(p. 133) When His saying, exalted is He, ﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Rum 15], in its various forms among the verses, indicated that this world is the abode of action, that the abode of the Hereafter is the abode of recompense, and that the barzakh (the intermediate realm between them) is a barrier between the two, so that neither of them contains what belongs to the other, He drew a consequence from that with His saying: ﴿So on that Day﴾, i.e., when the Hour arrives and this exchange takes place, ﴿their excuse will not benefit﴾, i.e., will not benefit at all, ﴿those who wronged﴾, i.e., those who put matters in other than their proper places, ﴿their excuse﴾. The excuse (ma'dhira) is that which establishes their pardon, namely the exertion of effort to find a plea that removes the shortcoming that has become apparent. (p. 134) They have no excuse, however hard they strive to establish one. The expression is extremely severe, since it indicates that whoever has committed any wrong at any time is in this condition. It also indicates that they will offer many excuses and much entreaty and great humbling of themselves, yet none of it will be accepted from them. This is according to the reading of the majority (al-Jama'a), with the verb in the feminine form, and it is more eloquent than the reading of the Kufans (al-Kufiyyun), with the verb in the masculine form, taking "excuse" as meaning "pleading." For if abundant excuse does not benefit, then a small amount of excuse, which is what the bare form indicates, will not benefit either, and not the reverse. It is possible that the reading of the majority is addressed to the disbelievers, and the reading of the Kufans to the disobedient among the believers, for among them are those whom excuse will benefit, so they are pardoned. What supports this is what has been transmitted concerning the last of the people of the Fire to leave it: he will ask that his face be turned away from it, and he will covenant with his Lord, glorified is He, that he will ask Him for nothing other than that. When He turns him away from that, he will see a great tree, and he will ask to be brought forward into its shade. Allah will say: "Did you not give covenants and pledges [that you would not ask]?" He will say: "Yes, my Lord! But do not let me be the most wretched of Your creation." The hadith continues: "And his Lord will excuse him." So his excuse has been accepted (p. 134) in general, but He does not require of him that he remove the blame, because that is not possible except through action, and the place of action has passed. Thus forgiveness comes from beyond all of that.

Since reproach is one of the customs of loved ones, He said: ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾, i.e., those who put matters in other than their proper places will not be asked, outwardly or inwardly, explicitly or by allusion, to remove what they have fallen into that calls for reproach, which is the displeasure arising from a shortcoming committed by the one being reproached. That is because this is possible only through obedience, and the place of obedience has passed, since the veil has been lifted, because the abode in which acts of obedience benefit is the abode of faith in the unseen, and it has ended. The expression indicates that the believers will be reproached with a reproach that gives them pleasure.

When this surah had made clear the paths of faith with the utmost clarity, and had cast upon the faces of the people of transgression the full extent of disgrace and humiliation, the sense of the discourse was: "We have brought forth in this surah in particular, after the generality of what is in the rest of the Qur'an, every proof before which comparisons cannot stand, and We have left no one with an excuse or any difficulty, because it has no parallel in its clarity." He connected to this by His words, turning the speech to the station of majesty, to condemn their opposition to what came before it, and to instil awe against taking [the warning] lightly, emphasising that they deny that there is any indication in the Qur'an. As for those among them who acknowledged it while remaining in disbelief, their disbelief stands in place of their denial: ﴿And We have certainly set forth﴾.

Since the care in this surah is more directed to people, He said: ﴿for mankind﴾, placing them first in the mention, ﴿in this Qur'an﴾, that is, in the whole of this surah and others, ﴿every kind of example﴾, that is, a strange meaning which is clearer and more established than the landmarks of mountains, in an expression which is more graceful than all other parables.

Since those upon whose hearing and perception a seal has been set among them do not believe in anything, and since that is one of the clearest proofs of His knowledge and power, He said, swearing an oath to refute their saying in their demands, particularly [addressing] the foremost of the people of knowledge and faith, to indicate that the disposing of hearts is of such great standing that it is beyond description, expressing it with the conditional, to inform that He, glory be to Him, is under no obligation to do anything, conjoining it to a sense of: "None of that benefited them": ﴿And if you were to bring them﴾, that is, to people in general, ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a clear indication of your truthfulness, a miracle, other than what you have brought them, of what they had demanded and promised to believe in, whether it was visible or audible, ﴿those who disbelieved would surely say﴾, that is, We have judged them to be disbelievers out of severity and harshness, and He indicated their extreme obstinacy by His words: ﴿Indeed [in]﴾, that is, "what" (ma) [...]. Since singling out [the disbelievers] for severity is harder on the self, He joined to it their followers, as consolation and as a clarification of the magnitude of their hostility, and so He said: ﴿You﴾, that is, O you who brought the sign, and his followers (p-136) ﴿are only falsifiers﴾, that is, of those skilled in falsehood (ʿarrāfa) by bringing what has no reality in the form of what has reality. As for those who believed, they say: "We are believers in this sign."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 30, verse 59:

Since it is among the most astonishing of wonders that one who claims intellect persists in denying the truth, does not give ear to proof, and does not find the way, he said, resuming in answer to one who asked him: "Would there be a seal like this?" and encouraging seeking knowledge: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like this exceedingly great sealing, and since the fact that one and the same thing is guidance for some people and misguidance for others, combining greatness with perfect knowledge and wisdom, he turned the address away from these to the Greatest Name, the all-encompassing, and said: ﴿Allah seals﴾, that is, He to whom none is equal, so whatever He wills comes to be, as a constant custom, and he drew attention to the multitude of those sealed upon by using the plural of multiplicity, and said: ﴿upon the hearts of those who do not know﴾, that is, they do not renew — that is, due to the absence of receptivity — the knowledge by not seeking the knowledge of what they are ignorant of, of what this Book has verified of the sciences of this world and the Hereafter, being content with what they have of ignorances they called indications, and misguidances they thought were guidances and perfections.

(p-137) Since this [verse] reminds [the Prophet] of the immensity of God's power after despair of their faith, He made His statement ﴿So be patient﴾ a consequence of it. That is, be patient in warning them despite this harshness, their rejection with falsehood, and [their] harm, for all of it is Our doing, and nothing in it escapes Our will.

Since it had already been decreed to him that his affair would certainly prevail over every affair, He gave the reason for it with His words, emphasizing it. The enforcement of such a matter, in a context of denial, given the greatness and multitude of the opponents, [is expressed] with an explicit noun rather than a pronoun, lest one think the promise is restricted to a condition of nature: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, [is fulfilled] in everything He promised you, which includes your victory and the manifestation of your religion over all religion, and the victory of those who come close to your followers in holding to a Book from the Books of Allah, even if it has been abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a earlier ruling by a later one) for those who have no Book. ﴿is true﴾, that is, firmly established, and matched by reality, as time reveals it, and as the vicissitudes of events bring it about.

Since the implied sense was "So do not hasten," He joined to it His words: ﴿and let not those who have no certainty make you unsteady﴾, that is, let them not move you to levity, nor seek to make you hasty by urging the hastening of victory out of fear of the consequences of its delay, or by making you slack in conveying [the message]. Rather, keep your distance from them through sternness and harshness, and by proclaiming the bitter truth without any partiality whatsoever, a distance such that they do not hope to find a way, by any kind of stratagem, to make you waver in this. The reading "yastahiqqannaka" (from haqq, "truth"), (p-138) its meaning being: that is, let them not demand from you the truth, which is the just decision between you and them. That is, do not demand it yourself. It is like [the expression] "Let me not see you here," where you forbid yourself while you wish to forbid him from being in a place where you can see him. The prohibition in the reading of the majority, with the heavy form (nun al-tawkid al-thaqilah, the emphatic nun), is stronger than in the transmission of Ruways from Ya'qub with the light form (nun al-tawkid al-khafifah). The reading of the majority is directed to the root of the religion, that is, do not act toward them in a way that makes them hope you will incline toward them in it. The reading of Ruways is directed toward wealth, for he would win them over by bestowing it upon them. There is no doubt that if he gave them preference over the great Muslims, this would encourage them to seek that he incline toward them. Nothing but a shift of the prohibition achieves this. Had it been said, "Do not be swayed with them," this would not convey that. Nor should one say the opposite, that the prohibition with the heavy nun is lighter because it forbids an emphasized act and so the basic act remains. 

Likewise, what is accompanied by light emphasis, and in the light form, which is not emphasized by heavy emphasis, leaves nothing but the basic act, so it is more eloquent, because the nun did not enter except after the forbidding verb had entered, so it adds only the strength of the prohibition, not the strength of the forbidden act. And Allah knows best.

﴿who have no certainty﴾, that is, the harm of those who do not believe in Our promises with a firm conviction in the heart. Rather, they are either doubters, for the slightest thing unsettles them, like one who worships Allah "on an edge" (Qur'an 22:11), or they deny Allah's victory for His believing friends and for those who come close to them in holding to a Book whose origin is sound. They exaggerate in enmity and denial, to the point that they gamble on Allah's promise of victory for the Romans over Persia, (p-139) as though they were certain and had insight into their affair that this would not happen. When Allah fulfills His promise in that matter by manifesting it soon, they will know their lie with their own eyes, and they will know, if they have any knowledge, that the promise of the Hour, for establishing justice upon the wrongdoer and returning good upon the doer of good, comes in the same way, and they will be humbled, and they will be gathered in abasement.

﴿And those who wronged will know what a [reversal] they will be returned to﴾ (Qur'an 26:227). Thus its last part is joined to its first, with the bending of a beloved to a beloved, and it is connected to it as a near one is connected to a near one, and it is fused as one kinsman is fused with another.
